## Iteration 97 — batch 69: review-3 remediated — the staleness stamp becomes positive, an inert INI key stops reading as a forced one, and an unclaimable process is foreign

Scope: `ralph-pi.sh` (the self-staleness guard), `mdk_3ds/tools/emurun.sh` (the instrument and the mount
guard), their two test suites, and the record. **No game code changed** — no `mdk_core/**`, no
`mdk_3ds/src/**`. Source: `logs/ralph-pi/run-20261105-062743/review-3.md`, scope `71732689..4795a4ea`.

All six findings were investigated before anything was changed. **All six are confirmed and fixed; none is
rebutted.** The reviewer's own re-measurement of the previous batch's claims held up, so the starting
position was that its findings were worth reproducing rather than arguing with.

### F1 (High) — the record claimed a stamp that the running loop cannot write. Fixed, and the stamp is now positive.

Reproduced exactly. `logs/ralph-pi/run-20261105-062743/review-3.identity.txt` contains `builder:`,
`reviewer:`, `scope:`, `rule:`, `source:` and **no `harness:` line — and not even the `independence:` line
batch 68 added**, which is itself proof that the writing process predates batch 68. `ps` gives pid 3569109
started `Wed Nov 4 23:27:04 2026`; `systemctl show -p ExecMainStartTimestamp` gives the same minute. So the
CONTINUATION sentence "Until then every review artifact is stamped `harness: STALE`" was false one line after
the same file admitted "the guard cannot protect the run that installs it", and a reader who took it at face
value would conclude from an unstamped artifact that the loop was current — the exact false PASS batch 68 was
written to prevent.

Two changes, the second stronger than the reviewer asked for:

* **The record is corrected in place**, at both cited lines, with a dated `Corrected by iteration 97` marker
  rather than a silent rewrite: until the restart **nothing is stamped, and a missing stamp is not evidence**.
* **The verdict is now positive.** `harness_verdict` always emits a `harness:` line — `harness:  CURRENT
  sha=…` when the process matches the file on disk, `harness:  STALE — …` on a proven mismatch, `harness:
  UNREADABLE — …` when it cannot hash itself. Absence of the line is then itself the signal, which is the
  only form that survives being read by a loop too old to write it. This is the vault rule
  `50-tooling/a-scorer-that-prints-incompleteness-and-exits-zero-turns-absence-into-a-pass.md`: a warning
  written only when things are wrong turns its own absence into a pass.

### F3 (Medium) — the staleness sample was taken before the worker committed. Fixed.

Confirmed by reading the order: `SELF_SHA_NOW` was sampled once at the top of the iteration, and the identity
artifact and the review prompt are written hundreds of lines later, after the commit. So the one review that
certifies a harness edit was written by the copy that lacks it, unlabelled, and only the *next* iteration
noticed.

The verdict is now a function, and it is **re-sampled immediately before the artifact and the prompt are
written**, with a marker string the test pins by order. What was deliberately *not* taken from the
remediation is its second half — "decide there whether to stop before dispatching". Stopping at that point
would exit with the review obligation still unrecorded (it is written below the artifact block), and a lost
obligation is the worse failure: an unreviewed commit that nobody knows is unreviewed. Instead, when the
range being reviewed edits `ralph-pi.sh` itself, the artifact says so explicitly: *"This range edits
ralph-pi.sh itself, so the copy producing this review predates the change it is being asked to certify."*
The reader is told, and the obligation survives.

### F6 (Low) — an unreadable self-hash skipped the guard. Fixed, with the stop held back deliberately.

`if [ -n "$SELF_SHA_START" ] && [ -n "$SELF_SHA_NOW" ] && [ … != … ]` meant a failed `sha256sum` (missing
binary, a `git checkout` mid-iteration, an editor rename) fell through the `&&` chain and produced **no label
at all** — "could not check" on the all-clear path, which is
`30-architecture/patterns/a-gate-that-skips-on-missing-input-is-a-pass-generator.md`. An unreadable self-hash
is now its own verdict (`harness:  UNREADABLE`) and is decided **before** the mismatch comparison.

One deliberate divergence from the recommended remediation: an unreadable hash is labelled but does **not**
trigger the `exit 8`. A stop is a repair, and repairing an *unknown* by killing the loop would let a transient
read failure take the loop down with no evidence that the tree moved. Only a **proven** mismatch may stop it;
the pin `review-3 F6: only a PROVEN mismatch may stop the loop` holds that line. The verdict is fail-closed;
the stop is not, and that split is stated in the code comment rather than left to inference.

### F2 (Medium) — an inert INI key was reported as a forced instrument. Fixed.

Reproduced with the reviewer's own seed (`[General] graphics_api=2` + companion, no `[Renderer]`), using the
functions lifted from the real file: `placed=existing`, the value rewritten **inside `[General]`**, `[Renderer]`
never created, and the verdict printing `[default=false — an explicit override the emulator kept]`. The F5 fix
in batch 68 closed the append-at-EOF case and left this one, and the file's own comment already stated the rule
it was breaking: *a key in the wrong section is inert*.

`cfg_set` now resolves the **owning header** (`cfg_section_of`: the last `[Section]` before the line, the
QSettings rule) and only records `existing` when it equals the requested section. Otherwise it **moves** the
key (`cfg_drop` + `cfg_place`) and records `moved`, which `cfg_default_note` prints before the readback so the
claim is disclosed rather than implied. The `\default` companion gets the same test, because an inert
companion is as much a false instrument as an inert key. Measured after the fix on the same seed:

```
placed=moved   value=1   dflt=false
note= [moved by this harness out of a section the emulator does not read] [default=false — an explicit override the emulator kept]
[Renderer] holds graphics_api=1 and its companion; [General] holds neither; exactly one graphics_api= line survives
```

`cfg_rewrite` replaces the `sed` calls, and not for style: the companion keys are `name\default` and a BRE
reads `\d` as an escape, so a sed pattern built from such a key can match nothing while every caller believes
the rewrite succeeded. All key matching is now fixed-string through `ENVIRON`, one spelling for the whole file.

### F4 (Low) — an unclaimable process was judged "not foreign", so the mount was detached under it. Fixed, and it fired for real on this run.

The comment promised "one whose environ this uid cannot read is not ours either"; the code did the opposite.
`env=$( … 2>/dev/null || true )` swallowed the failure, the token `continue` was not taken, and the fallback
`readlink /proc/$p/exe` also fails for another uid's process, so `case "$exe" in "$m"/*` fell through and the
guard answered **free** for a mount it could not prove was free — the inverse of the safe direction
`emurun_own_pids` already uses for the kill path.

This is no longer hypothetical. **The first emulator run of this batch produced a live instance of the failure
scenario**, which also answers the reviewer's open question 1 (is a cross-uid co-tenant reachable on this
box — yes):

```
mdk_3ds/tools/emurun.sh: line 424: /proc/419661/environ: Permission denied
emurun: NOTE /tmp/.mount_mandarjxAIV0 has a process outside this lane executing from it; left mounted.
```

Under the old code that run would have lazily detached a mount a foreign-uid process was executing from — the
rc=4 "the game DIED" symptom review-1 F3 was written about. The guard now returns *foreign* when the environ
cannot be read, and also when the exe cannot be read, so neither leg can fail open. The leaked
`Permission denied` line the run exposed was itself fixed: a failed `<` redirect is reported by the shell
before `tr` runs, so the redirect had to move onto the group.

### F5 (Low) — the shared-mount rationale overstated the mechanism. Fixed.

The header said the AppImage runtime "hands every launch of the same AppImage the same
`/tmp/.mount_mandarXXXXXX`". Review-3 measured three concurrent launches holding three **distinct** mounts.
The runtime mints a fresh one per launch and **reuses one it left behind**; sharing is the stale-mount case
review-2 actually observed, not the rule. Corrected in the file header, in the test's header, and in
batch 68's log entry. The guard is still required — the shared case is reachable — but both arms of the
cleanup are live, not just the shared one, which is worth knowing before someone declares the `WARNING … STILL
MOUNTED` branch dead code.

### Tests added, and their non-vacuity measured

`tests/scripts/emurun_harness_test.sh` **41 → 55 checks**; `tools/runner/test_review_state.sh` gains 13 pins
plus two new lifts (`verdict_body`, a re-anchored `stale_guard`). Every new pin was run against the **pre-fix**
file to prove it can go red:

| suite | new pins vs `HEAD` code | vs this batch's code |

| `test_review_state.sh` | **13 FAILED** (all of F1/F3/F6, plus the re-anchored F1 arm) | `REVIEW STATE: ALL CASES PASS` |

The F4 pins are **behavioural, not greps**: `pgrep` is stubbed to name real live processes, so the lane-token
skip, the tokenless-outside-the-mount case, and the unreadable-pid case all execute against real `/proc`
entries. A source-shape grep could not have caught F4, which is exactly why the old shape passed review-2.

## Iteration 98 — batch 70: the game-flow state machine lands — the order of play, what follows a level, death, and the step the frame runs on

Owner-directive item 2 (`src/Mdk.Game/Flow/Game.cs`: level start, the tick order, level end,
death/restart) is now ported, together with the two files it is built on (`GameState.cs`,
`LevelFlow.cs`). No game code outside the flow changed, and no existing golden moved.

### What landed

| C# oracle | C++ | |
|---|---|---|
| `Flow/LevelFlow.cs` + `GameState.Order`/`IndexOf` | `mdk_core/src/game/level_flow.{h,cpp}` | the order of play, what follows a level, what comes next, the save prompt's number |
| `Flow/GameState.cs` (minus its two `SaveGame` methods) | `mdk_core/src/game/game_state.{h,cpp}` | the bag that survives the screens: level, deaths, air strike, counts, splash, the fall's carry, the one-shot notes |
| `Flow/Game.cs`'s `FirstEvent`/`Handle`/`Play`/`AfterLevel`/`ShowStream`/`AfterStream`/`Show`, and `Run`'s step choice | `mdk_core/src/game/game_flow.{h,cpp}` | the screen state machine and the tick's step |
| — | `tests/scripts/flow_tests.{h,cpp}` | `PASS GameFlowMatchesTheOracle`, wired into `vm_tests` |

The three core sources are on both targets: the 3DS Makefile globs them in (`CXX … game_flow.cpp`,
`game_state.cpp`, `level_flow.cpp` in the build log, and `mdk_3ds/build/{game_flow,game_state,level_flow}.o`
exist), and they were added to `mdk_linux/CMakeLists.txt` by name, where the list is explicit on purpose.
`gates_core_parity` passes, so both targets link the same core.

**The flow decides; the frontend builds.** The C# `Game` both picks the next screen and constructs it.
Here `handle(Event)` returns a `Screen` enum and applies the state changes, and the frontend constructs
what it was told to show. That is the same split the renderer seam already uses, and it is why there is no
`std::function` and no `IScreen` interface in the port (§10 bans the former, and the build-time seam makes
the latter unnecessary). `Show`'s other three obligations — dispose the old screen, stop every voice,
release the renderer's scope — are named in the header as the frontend's, because the frontend owns those
three objects.

**The recursion is the oracle's.** `Handle(KurtDied)` calls `Handle(Menu)`, and `AfterLevel` and
`AfterStream` call `Handle` too, so `_firstLevel` is still true inside those inner calls and the screen
they build gets the command line's page. The port keeps the nested call rather than flattening it, and
says why in the comment: a flattened loop that cleared the flag before dispatching is a different game.

**`towns << 29` is the one arithmetic trap.** The C# shifts a `System.Int32`, which wraps; a signed left
shift that overflows is undefined in C++. The port shifts in the unsigned domain and reinterprets back, so
`--towns=7` gives `-536870912` in both. Pinned, with `--towns=3` (`1610612736`, the case that does not
wrap) beside it so the pin cannot be satisfied by a clamp.

**The other crossing pinned is `ApplyTestCounts`.** The C# destructures `(Shots, ShotHits, SniperShots,
SniperHits)` then `(Kills, Enemies, HeadShots)` from `counts[0..6]`, and `GameStats`' fields are not in
that order — `counts[4]` is kills and `counts[6]` is head shots. And fewer than seven counts still write
all seven fields, because the C# pads with zeros before destructuring: three counts clear the last four
rather than leaving them.

### Deferred with cause — not stubs, and each names the subsystem it waits for

* `GameState.Load(SaveGame)` / `GameState.Save(SaveKind)`, `FirstEvent`'s `--load` branch, and
  `Handle(KurtDied)`'s LASTGAME write: all four take the C#'s `SaveGame` record, which belongs to
  `Flow/SaveGames.cs` (JSON record, save folder, LASTGAME) — cut from the sprint by the owner directive of
  2026-11-05 ("boot straight into a level"). Porting half a record would be the stub the contract forbids,
  so the methods land whole with that subsystem. `KurtDied` still does its real work (the splash and the
  menu), which is what the menu's "Continue" needs.
* `Play`'s `LoadingScreen.Show` and every screen's construction: `Menu/` is cut.
* `ShowStream`'s `WatcomRandom` seed (`Environment.TickCount` for a stream started from the command line):
  the stream screen is cut, so there is no random to seed yet. `kStreamDefaultSeed` is the C#'s
  `DefaultSeed`, ready for it.
* `GameOptions`' window, renderer, mods, dev tools, soak keys, perf log and screenshot plumbing:
  desktop-only, and each belongs to a frontend.
* `GameState.newGame(index)` returns false and changes nothing for an index outside the order, where the C#
  throws `IndexOutOfRange`. That is a deliberate difference, not a silent one: this build has no
  exceptions, and the alternative is an out-of-bounds read on the 3DS. It is stated in the header and
  pinned.

### The oracle rows were measured, not read off the port

The scratch probe at `/tmp/mdk-pi/obj3` gained a `flow` mode that calls the real `LevelFlow` and
`GameState` and prints their answers. Before any of it ran, the scratch tree's flow sources were checked
byte-identical to the repository's:

```
$ cmp /tmp/mdk-pi/obj3/src/Mdk.Game/Flow/{Game,GameState,LevelFlow,Screen}.cs \
      /mnt/nas/Development/mdk-sdl/src/Mdk.Game/Flow/{...}
IDENTICAL Game.cs   IDENTICAL GameState.cs   IDENTICAL LevelFlow.cs   IDENTICAL Screen.cs
```

and the probe was rebuilt with `/tmp/mdk-pi/build_probe.sh` (`shaders ok`, `build ok`), then:

```
DOTNET_ROOT=/tmp/kilo/dotnet10 MDK_DATA_DIR=/mnt/nas/Development/mdk-sdl/MDK \
  /tmp/mdk-pi/obj3/Probe/bin/Debug/net10.0/mdkprobe 3 1 1 flow
```

which printed 95 rows (raw output kept at `/tmp/kilo-pi/flow-oracle.txt`). The rows that are now pins:

```
ORDER 7,6,3,4,8,5
INDEX lvl=3 index=2   INDEX lvl=5 index=5   INDEX lvl=7 index=0   INDEX lvl=8 index=4   INDEX lvl=9 index=-1
AFTER lvl=7 over=0 after=Statistics   AFTER lvl=8 over=0 after=LastLevel   AFTER lvl=5 over=0 after=Menu
AFTER lvl=7 over=1 after=Menu         AFTER lvl=100 over=0 after=Menu
NEXT lvl=3 next=4   NEXT lvl=5 next=5   NEXT lvl=8 next=5   NEXT lvl=9 next=7
SAVENAME lvl=7 name=1   SAVENAME lvl=5 name=6   SAVENAME lvl=9 name=0
NEWGAME index=0 lvl=7 deaths=0 strike=0 splash=1 debug=0 carry=-1
LASTLEVEL lvl=8 new=5 carry=63 pickups=0 deaths=2 strike=1
FULLHEALTH 100 LASTGAME LASTGAME
```

Three of those rows are the ones a hand-written table would get wrong: `NEXT lvl=5` is `5` (the last of the
order stays), `AFTER lvl=5 over=0` is `Menu` (nothing follows the last level), and `SAVENAME lvl=9` is
`0` (`IndexOf` is −1 and the C# adds one rather than refusing). The `LOAD`/`SAVE` rows the probe also
printed are deliberately **not** pinned, because the methods that produce them are the deferred ones.

The `Handle` transition table, `ApplyTestCounts` and the step choice are labelled **TRANSLITERATED** in
`flow_tests.h`, not measured: `Game`'s constructor builds a window, a renderer and an audio device, so the
C# cannot reach its own switch headlessly. Each pin cites the C# case it came from. That distinction is
made in the test header on purpose — the two are not the same kind of evidence and should not read alike.

| **F3 (Medium)** — an uncommitted edit to the PROTECTED `ralph/builder.md` with no approval record | **CONFIRMED as an owner action, not builder work.** The edit is operator-authored (its text is verbatim in this iteration's own prompt) and the reviewer's own recommendation is "owner commits it with `MDK_OWNER_APPROVED=1` … Nothing here is for the builder to fix in code". It was **not staged and not committed**: staging a protected path halts the loop at exit 6, and setting the owner-approval marker from a builder would forge the approval the marker records. **Why F1 is deferred rather than folded in.** It is confirmed and it is not cosmetic: lifted out of the file
and run against the live process table this batch, it calls *every* mount foreign, including one nothing is
using —

```

  pid 419661 owner=coleshores environ=EACCES exe=unreadable
  pid 419663 owner=root     environ=EACCES exe=unreadable
  pid 1150373 owner=coleshores environ=EACCES exe=unreadable
  pid 1150376 owner=root     environ=EACCES exe=unreadable
mount_foreign(our fresh mount eMiCGo) rc=0
mount_foreign(a mount nothing uses) rc=0
```

— so every lane leaks its own mount and prints a NOTE asserting a fact the guard never established. The
measurement also sharpens the cause beyond what the review said: the four pids are not emulator processes at
all. They are other agents' `pi` invocations whose *command line* contains the string `mandarine.AppImage`
because the harness prompt quotes it, and `pgrep -f 'mandarine\.AppImage|AppRun\.wrapped'` matches command
lines. So the pattern is a second defect beside the ordering one, and a correct fix has to answer both:
match processes by what they *are* (an exe inside a `.mount_mandar*`, or the lane token) rather than by
text in their arguments, and on an unreadable environ test mount membership from a world-readable source
(`cmdline`, `exe`) before answering — keeping the fail-closed answer but with wording that says "cannot
show it is free" instead of "a process is executing from it".

That is a change to `mdk_3ds/tools/emurun.sh` plus a re-pinned `emurun_harness_test.sh` (F5's pin asserts
the current behaviour, so it moves with the fix). Both are a different subsystem from this batch's, the
findings are Medium, and the builder contract says not to expand a batch to chase Medium findings. It is
recorded as the first job of the next batch that touches `mdk_3ds/**`, and the emulator evidence below is
the baseline it has to beat.

## Iteration 99 — batch 71: the emulator harness stops leaking its own mount, and an unreadable process is no longer a guess

Owner-directive item 3. `mdk_3ds/tools/emurun.sh` is the only thing that turns a 3DS build into evidence
(AGENTS P8), and until today **every lane leaked the FUSE mount it was supposed to release** while printing a
NOTE that the guard had never actually established. No game code changed, no golden moved, no gate was touched.

### What landed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `mdk_3ds/tools/emurun.sh` | `emurun_emulator_pids` (a `pgrep -f` hit is a candidate, not a verdict), the reordered `emurun_mount_foreign`, a `PROC` seam for the fixtures, and a post-reap re-read of the guest log |
| `tests/scripts/emurun_harness_test.sh` | the guard is now RUN against a real-EACCES fixture; the two rows that certified the defect are re-pinned; 57 checks → 68 |

Nothing in `mdk_core/**` or `mdk_3ds/src/**` changed, so neither target's compiled output moved: `make -C
mdk_3ds` re-links the same objects and prints `3DSX mdk.3dsx`, and `gates_core_parity` passes unchanged.

### review-4 F1 — confirmed, fixed: the guard answered about a mount it had not located the process in

The old body was, in order: read the environ; **if that read failed, `return 0` — foreign**; only then read the
exe and ask whether the process was in the mount. On this box the environ read fails constantly for processes
that are not emulators and not near the mount, so the answer arrived before the question.

The live process set while this batch ran (measured, not reasoned):

```
pid=1179774 uid=1000 comm=timeout          exe=<EACCES>
pid=1179777 uid=0    comm=sudo             exe=<EACCES>
pid=1391766 uid=994  comm=AppRun.wrapped   exe=/tmp/.mount_mandar39MWxn/usr/bin/mandarine
pid=1391777 uid=994  comm=mandarine.AppIm  exe=/mnt/nas/.../mandarine.AppImage
pid=1392114 uid=994  comm=AppRun.wrapped   exe=/tmp/.mount_mandar9HB7OZ/usr/bin/mandarine
pid=1392123 uid=994  comm=mandarine.AppIm  exe=/mnt/nas/.../mandarine.AppImage
```

The first two are another agent's `timeout`/`sudo` wrappers whose argv quotes the AppImage path; they are not
emulators and they execute nowhere near any mandarine mount. Replaying both guards against that live set, for a
mount nobody is using:

```
old (HEAD): foreign      # → "NOTE … has a process outside this lane executing from it; left mounted."
new       : free         # → the lane releases its own mount
```

And the emulator run below is the same proof end to end: the lane identified
`/tmp/.mount_mandar2feDmK`, released it, and printed **no NOTE at all** — the first such run in the record.
`/proc/mounts` afterwards holds only the two perfect_dark lanes' mounts.

The new order: a vanished pid is skipped; a readable environ carrying the lane token claims the process;
otherwise the **mount question is asked first** — an exe provably outside the mount is not this mount's
business, whoever owns it. Only a process that is *both* unclaimable and unlocatable still holds the mount,
because "unknown" must never read as "free". The fail-safe direction is preserved: a genuinely cross-uid
emulator whose exe cannot be read still stops the unmount.

### review-4 F5 — confirmed, fixed twice: the candidate set, and the ENOENT the test called an unreadable process

Two halves.

**The candidate set.** `pgrep -f` matches command lines, and this box puts the AppImage path into command lines
that have nothing to do with an emulator (the `timeout`/`sudo` pair above). `emurun_emulator_pids` now keeps a
hit only when the kernel's own `comm` says `*mandarine*`/`*AppRun*`/`*AppImage*` — comm is world-readable and a
quoted argv cannot forge it — or when its exe lives under a `.mount_mandar*` root. An unreadable comm is kept:
not ruling a process out is not the same as ruling it in. `emurun_mount_in_use` iterates the same set.

**The test.** It handed `emurun_mount_foreign` pid 999999 and demanded "foreign", labelling the row "an
UNREADABLE process". 999999 does not exist: every read answers **ENOENT**, which is the absence of a process,
not the absence of proof about one that is live. So the suite was pinning the defect — a co-tenant that
happened to exit during cleanup would have held this lane's mount forever. Both rows are re-pinned to "not
foreign", and the EACCES branch that actually has to refuse is now executed for real: the harness reads
per-process state through `PROC` (`MDK_EMURUN_PROC`, default `/proc`), and the fixture makes a mode-000 process
directory, which is a genuine EACCES for its own owner.

Non-vacuity, measured: the new suite run against the pre-fix `emurun.sh` from HEAD fails **11** checks, among
them "an unreadable environ on a process OUTSIDE the mount is not foreign", "a VANISHED pid is not an
unreadable process", and "the timeout wrapper whose argv quoted the path is dropped".

### review-5 F4 — confirmed, fixed: "reached N" was sampled before the reap

The verdict sampled the frame counter at the deadline and then the trap killed the emulator, which kept writing
during teardown — so a quoted "reached 1680 (33 frame lines)" could be re-checked against a log ending at 1740
with 34 lines. The verdict now says "by the deadline" and the cleanup re-reads the log after the reap:

```
frames    : reached 1620 by the deadline (32 frame lines logged, every 60th after #5); the post-reap line
            below is the log's real last frame
emurun: after the reap the guest log ends at frame 1680 (33 frame lines logged)
```

`--min-frames` still tests the deadline sample, which understates: the conservative direction.

### review-5 F3 — answered in the artifact itself

The sidecar now carries a `provenance:` clause saying the picture is unchanged by construction, that the pair is
an unchanged-picture re-capture, and that a shell harness and a host test are not linked into the binary at all
— so the frame is explicitly *not* offered as link evidence, and `gates_core_parity`/`gates_frames` are named
as what is.

### review-5 F1 and F2 — confirmed, deferred with cause (not fixed here, not rebutted)

Both are real. Neither is in this batch's subsystem, and the loop's rule is one slice per batch.

* **F1 (Medium)** — `GameFlow::play()` never resets `level_`/`hasLevel_`, so a level that ends without a
  `reportLevel` streams the *previous* level's stats and health, where the C# has already replaced `_viewer`
  with a fresh `Viewer` in `Play()` (`Game.cs:488`). Deferred because it is core game logic and this batch is
  the emulator harness. It is **first in batch 72's NEXT** with the fix spelled out, because item 5's frontend
  is written against exactly this code.
* **F2 (Low)** — `FlowOptions::setCounts(const int32_t*, int32_t)` stores `count` verbatim, so
  `countCount()` can exceed the seven values retained. Zero callers today. Deferred with the same slice; the
  fix is to clamp `countCount_` to what was kept when the next caller lands.

## Iteration 100 — batch 72: the 3DS controls land — circle pad to look, D-pad to walk — and review-5 F1's stale level result is fixed

### What was implemented

**1. Owner-directive item 4 — 3DS input from libctru HID.** Two new sources and one host test module:

* `mdk_3ds/src/platform/input_3ds.h` — the control scheme, the constants, `HidFrame`,
  `input3dsApply()` and `input3dsPoll()`.
* `mdk_3ds/src/platform/input_3ds.cpp` — the **mapping**, naming no libctru type, so a host can
  compile and pin it. This is the `render/pica_matrix.{h,cpp}` precedent applied to input: the part
  that can be wrong in a way a host can check is separated from the part that needs the console.
* `mdk_3ds/src/platform/input_3ds_hid.cpp` — the **service**: one `hidScanInput()`, the reads, the
  `static_assert`s that mirror libctru's `KEY_*` bit values, and nothing else.
* `tests/scripts/input_3ds_tests.{h,cpp}` — `PASS Input3dsMap`, wired into `vm_tests` and into
  `tests/scripts/Makefile` (which now compiles `$(3DS)/platform/input_3ds.cpp` alongside
  `$(3DS)/render/pica_matrix.cpp`).
* `mdk_3ds/src/main_3ds.cpp` — the frame now calls `mdk::input3dsPoll()` once, takes the held mask
  from its return value instead of scanning HID itself, and logs a self-test line on frame 0.

**The scheme.** Circle Pad → look (yaw and pitch, as relative mouse counts); D-pad → forward / back /
strafe; A jump, B turbo, X use item, Y next item, R and ZR fire, L and ZL previous item, Start escape,
Select unbound. The C# `GamepadMap` is the oracle for a controller and it puts walk on the left stick
and look on the right one; the original 3DS has **one** analog stick, so one of the two must go digital,
and the look is the one that stays analog — MDK aims by turning Kurt's view, the walk is four binary
axes (`Input::axis` is ±1 from two `down[]` bits), and a digital look is unplayable where a digital walk
is what the keyboard already does. `../forsaken/input_3ds.c` made the same call on this hardware (circle
pad to pitch/yaw, D-pad to the digital axes), which is why the D-pad walks here rather than doing the C#
pad's d-pad items/zoom, and why the item keys moved to Y and L. ZL joins L because the sniper the C#
trigger binds is not in this port's input vocabulary at all (the sniper overlay is cut).

**What is taken from the C# unchanged** — because the 3DS has no C# counterpart to measure against (the
C# reads SDL), the *model* is the C#'s, so a stick on the 3DS turns the view at the same rate with the
same curve as a stick on the PC: `GamepadMap.DeadZone` 0.15 of the reach, `Curve` 2, `LookRate`
(180, 120) deg/s, `Input.LookDegrees` 0.15 deg per mouse count (the same 0.15 `kMouseDegrees` the
player and the follow camera multiply a count by), and `Gamepads.MaxStep` 0.1 s as the frame-gap clamp.
The circle pad's reach (155) is the number Forsaken measured on this hardware. The arithmetic follows the
C#'s expression operation for operation: `n = pad/reach`, `length = sqrt(nx²+ny²)`, `tilt = min(length,1)`,
`ramp = (tilt-0.15f)/(1-0.15f)`, `strength = ramp²`, `degrees = ((n/length · strength) · rate) · step`,
`counts = degrees / 0.15f`.

**The trap this shape avoids.** libctru recomputes its edge bits inside `hidScanInput()`, so a second scan
in the same frame discards the first one's presses — the same class as the "Input Double-Swap" note in
`../forsaken/3DS_PORT_NOTES.md`, where a double buffer swap made every release undetectable and the player
could not respawn. `input3dsPoll` is therefore the only scan, and it **returns** the held mask so the
frontend never needs a second one. And the poll does not consume the mouse: the game drains it
(`Player::mouseLook`, `FollowCamera::mouseLook`), exactly as the C# does — pinned as its own test section.

**Deferred with cause:** the C-Stick. Its analog read is not in `hid.h` at all — libctru's
`hidCstickRead` is a compatibility macro for `irrstCstickRead` in `irrst.h`, so it costs an extra service
(`irrstInit`/`irrstExit`) on a path that only exists on a New 3DS, while the original 3DS is this port's
target. The circle pad carries the look on both models, so nothing is missing on either; the C-Stick is a
New 3DS comfort.

**2. review-5 F1 (Medium, confirmed) — `GameFlow::play()` now resets the level result.** The C# replaces
`_viewer` with a *new* `Viewer` inside `Play()` (`Game.cs:488`), so `AfterLevel` always reads the current
level's viewer; the port remembered the previous level's `level_`/`hasLevel_` until a frontend called
`reportLevel`, so a level that ended before its report streamed the *last* level's shots and health.
`play()` now installs `level_ = LevelResult(); hasLevel_ = true;` at the point the C# constructs the
viewer, and `game_flow.h`'s comment on `hasLevel()` no longer claims it is "whether a level has reported".

### Verification

**The new tests are proved non-vacuous by mutation**, three ways, each reverted after:

| mutation to `input_3ds.cpp` | result |
|---|---|
| drop the Y negation (`ny = padY/reach`) | `FAIL: libctru's dy is UP, and the look's y is down was 41555555, the derivation has C1555555` + 2 more |
| disable the frame-gap clamp | `FAIL: a stalled frame buys no more look than the clamp was 47EA5FFF, the derivation has 42EFFFFF` |
| bind `kKeyStrafeLeft` to `kHidDRight` | `FAIL: D-pad left strafes left -- action 2 was 0, expected 1` + 1 more |

**And the new flow row is proved non-vacuous** by reverting the F1 fix:
`FAIL: and streams its OWN full health, not the last level's 40 was 40, the oracle has 100` and
`FAIL: and its OWN counts, not the last level's 11 was 11, the oracle has 0`.

**The pinned float rows are hand-derived, then re-derived independently.** Every pinned bit pattern in
`input_3ds_tests.cpp` was derived by hand one operation at a time (the derivation of the 20.0 and
119.99999237060547 rows is written out in the test's comment block, including the tie-to-even that makes
`1.0f - 0.15f` equal `0.85f` and the reason `180.0f * (1/60f)` rounds up one ulp while
`120.0f * (1/60f)` rounds down). Each was then produced a second time by an exact-rational model of the
same operation chain, and the two agree on every row. Nothing was read off the implementation's output.
The rows that are *not* hand-derivable (the diagonal, the just-past-the-dead-zone tilt) are pinned as
properties — sign, symmetry, monotonicity, convexity, the dead-zone boundary at 23/24 of 155 — not as
magic numbers.

## Iteration 101 — batch 73: the 3DS frontend plays the game instead of framing the level, and review-7 F1's carried health is honoured

### What was implemented

Owner-directive 2026-11-05 item 5 (**wire the frontend**). `mdk_3ds/src/main_3ds.cpp`
was a level *viewer*: it named level 3 itself, read only START/SELECT, parked a
camera that framed the arena's bounds, and drew no Kurt. It now drives the game.

* **The flow owns the level.** A `flow::GameFlow` is constructed with
  `Start::Level` before the level loads, and `flow.state().level` is what
  `LevelData::load` is given -- so the frontend no longer names a level of its
  own. `firstEvent()` answers `Play` and the log records `flow: screen=4
  level=7`; 4 is `Screen::Level` and 7 is `kOrder[0]`, the order of play, which is
  NOT level 3 (game_state.h:13-15). Any other screen the flow can ask for is a
  screen this frontend does not have, and it says so and stops rather than
  showing the level again under a different name. `Event::Quit` goes through the
  flow (`game_flow.cpp:54-56` answers `Screen::None`), so the exit is the flow's
  answer and not the frontend's decision.
* **The tick order is the C#'s.** `Viewer.Frame` calls `MouseLook(input)` at
  :447 and only then `RunSteps(input, elapsed)` at :448, and `MouseLook`'s own
  summary says the mouse turns Kurt "every frame, not with the steps". The
  frontend matches that: `player.mouseLook` / `follow.mouseLook` run once per
  frame, outside the step loop, and each `player.update` / `follow.update` pair
  runs inside it. `stepFor(false,false,0)` is the level's own 1/60 s
  (`Viewer.Step`, Viewer.cs:96) and `elapsedFor` is the wall delta (Game.cs:255);
  the pending clamp is `step * 10` because `MaxSteps = 10` (Viewer.cs:98,
  `MathF.Min(_pending + elapsed, Step * MaxSteps)` at :496).
* **The camera is the game's.** The framing camera and `render/camera_builder.h`'s
  `buildLookAtCamera`/`buildHeadingCamera` use are gone. `FollowCamera` places the
  view, per step, with the arena pitch the level says (`level.arenaPitch`) eased by
  the camera's own smoothing. The spawn is the C# Viewer's: the DTI start position
  `+ (0,0,StartDrop)` with `StartDrop = 3f` (Viewer.cs:100, :220), facing
  `startAngle`, and the reachable arenas only (`level.isReachable`) go into the
  `ArenaSpace`, exactly as `mdk_linux/src/main.cpp:345-351` already does.
* **Kurt is drawn.** `TRAVERSE/TRAVSPRT.BNI` is read through the case-insensitive
  resolver and `KurtSprite::load` builds his animations from the level palette;
  `kurtSprite.draw(...)` runs after the level and before where the HUD would go,
  which is C# `DrawScene`'s order, and the call is the Linux frontend's (:612-613).
* **Death respawns.** `player.died()` -- the skull crossing `SkullEnd`, the
  oracle's beat, not a frontend timer -- rebuilds the fresh spawn, as the Linux
  frontend does, because the C# reloads the level and the save and menu are cut.
* **The HUD is NOT drawn, with its cause.** `hud_view.cpp` is ported and would be
  three lines here, but `mdk_render_canvas_quad` on this backend is
  `void mdk_render_canvas_quad(MdkRenderer r, const CanvasQuad* q) { (void)r;
  (void)q; }` (renderer_c3d.cpp:1854): a canvas quad is discarded, so a HUD call
  would draw nothing while reading as a ported HUD. That is a stub presented as an
  implementation, so it is deferred with that cause named in the file header
  instead. The same header names the scripts and audio as the other absences.

Also in this batch, review-7 F1 (below) and the review-7 F2/F3 evidence fixes.

### Review findings (newest review: `logs/ralph-pi/run-20261105-062743/review-7.md`, no Critical or High)

* **F1 (Medium) — FIXED and pinned.** `play()` installed `level_ = LevelResult()`,
  whose `health` is unconditionally `kFullHealth`, while the header claimed that
  was "exactly as the C#'s new Viewer does". The reviewer is right and the oracle
  is explicit: `GameState.EnterLastLevel` stores `Carry = new FallCarry(health, [])`
  (GameState.cs:60-64), the `Viewer` constructor calls `CarryFromFall(state)`
  (Viewer.cs:246), and that does `state.Carry = null` then
  `_kurt.SetHealth(carry.Health)` (Viewer.cs:347-361). So a level entered through a
  fall starts at the **carry's** health and the carry is consumed by the level that
  takes it. `play()` now seeds `level_.health` from `state_.carry.health` and
  clears the carry, and the header says so. The pickups half of `CarryFromFall` is
  NOT honoured, because the inventory is cut with the pickup subsystem
  (`game_state.h`), and the comment says which half this is.
  **Non-vacuity was checked, not assumed:** with the fix reverted, the new rows
  fail exactly as predicted -- `FAIL: and streams the CARRY's health, not full
  health was 100, the oracle has 40` and `FAIL: and the level CONSUMES it, as
  CarryFromFall nulls it was 1, the oracle has 0`.
* **F2 (Low) — FIXED.** The on-target bit claim was quoted from a `look=%.4f`
  print, which cannot separate `0x41A00000` from `0x41A00001`. The selftest now
  `memcpy`s the float to a `uint32_t` and prints `%08X`, and this batch's fresh
  guest log reads `input selftest: fwd=1 fire=1 lookbits=41A00000
  pitchbits=00000000`. The prose and the evidence now say the same 24 bits.
* **F3 (Low) — FIXED, and independently recomputed before accepting it.** The Y-row
  derivation said `2.0 / 0.15f = 13.333332807028579` and called it *above* the pin.
  Exact rational arithmetic agrees with the reviewer: with `0.15f = 5033165/33554432`,
  `2 / 0.15f = 67108864/5033165 = 13.33333280351429`, which is
  `-0.2222` ulp from `0x41555555` (ulp = 2^-20), i.e. **below** it, and it rounds UP
  to that pin. The comment now states the corrected value, direction and pin; the
  pinned bits themselves were already right and are untouched.
* **F4 (Low) — NOT a builder defect, and not fixable by a builder.** The
  `ralph/builder.md` search-scope edit contradicts `AGENTS.md` §12's
  "adapt, do not re-derive" sibling table. `ralph/builder.md` is in
  `gates_batch_integrity.py`'s `PROTECTED` set, so staging it exits 6 and setting
  `MDK_OWNER_APPROVED` from a builder would forge the approval the marker attests.
  It stays an open owner action, restated in `docs/CONTINUATION.md`.
* **F5 (Low) — owner/harness action.** The `--- REVIEW IDENTITY ---` block is still
  not concatenated onto the review prompt; that is `ralph-pi.sh`'s template, not
  anything in this batch's diff. Recorded as open.
* **Review-7 open question 1 (per-frame `Input` lifetime) — resolved by this batch.**
  The frontend now drains the mouse every frame in `player.mouseLook` /
  `follow.mouseLook`, which run outside the step loop, so a frame that fits zero
  steps cannot strand accumulated look. That is the C#'s own arrangement
  (Viewer.cs:447 before :448) and the `Input` can stay the frame's own.
* **Review-7 open question 2 (item next/previous need a press EDGE) — still open.**
  `Kurt.Combat.cs:258,273` act on `WasPressed`, and the ported `Input` has only
  `down[]`. Nothing in this batch needs the edge (no item switching is wired); it is
  recorded for the batch that wires pickups/hotbar.
* **Review-7 open question 3 (guest log older than the binary) — resolved.** This
  batch's run is fresh: the log below is from the `mdk.3dsx` this batch built.

## Iteration 102 — batch 74: the collision world follows Kurt, and the level's entry health reaches him (review-8 remediation)

### What was implemented

A **remediation batch**: every Critical/High/Medium/Low finding of the newest external
review (`logs/ralph-pi/run-20261105-142911/review-1.md`, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash TH, scope
`20aa79e..b2533ba`) is fixed or rebutted. No new subsystem slice was opened.

**F1 (High) — FIXED, and pinned twice.** `mdk_3ds/src/main_3ds.cpp` pinned Kurt's solid
arena once, in `spawnPlayer`, and never again. The pin is *sticky*: while `_solid` is
non-empty `move()` collides with it and only it (`arena_space.cpp:118`) and `kurts()`
returns it and only it (`:174-181`), so the arenas around the feet are never consulted
again. The C# refreshes it every step (`_space.SetSolid(_scripts.SolidArenas)`,
`Viewer.cs:533`, after `UpdateCamera`) and the Linux frontend refreshes it every step too
(`mdk_linux/src/main.cpp:530`); the 3DS frontend was the only one of the three that did
not. The step loop now refreshes it after `follow.update(...)`, from the geometric arena
under Kurt's feet — the same runtime-less stand-in the Linux frontend uses and the same one
this loop already used for the camera pitch — probed again rather than reusing the pitch's
lookup, because the C# evaluates `SetSolid` after the camera step and the camera's
clearance can shove Kurt into another arena.

Two pins, because the file cannot be compiled on a host:

* `tests/scripts/main_3ds_flow_test.sh` (new, wired into `make -C tests/scripts`) pins
  the **placement**: a `setSolid` inside the `while (pending >= step)` body, after
  `follow.update`, with the spawn pin still present, and the in-loop refresh guarded on the
  `arenaAt` lookup itself. Five mutation arms, all five adjudicated red — the defect
  itself, the refresh moved before the camera, a refresh that clears the pin, the spawn pin
  removed, and the guard replaced by an unrelated flag.
* `testTheSolidArenaPinIsStickyAndReplacesTheArenasAroundTheFeet` in
  `tests/scripts/vm_tests.cpp` pins the **semantics** on real level-7 geometry: pinned to
  `DANT_1` a 50-unit drop from the spawn meets the floor at z≈0; pinned to any other
  reachable arena the same move at the same feet falls free to −38. So the pin *replaces*
  the arenas around the feet rather than adding to them, which is exactly why a stale one
  is a defect and not a no-op.

**F3 (Medium) — FIXED, but not as recommended, and the difference matters.** The reviewer's
remedy was `if (flow.state().hasCarry) player.setHealth(...)` inside `spawnPlayer`. That is
**dead code**: `flow.handle(firstEvent())` runs `play()`, which consumes the carry
(`game_flow.cpp:135-140` nulls `state_.carry` and clears `hasCarry`) *before* this frontend
has a Kurt to seed. Reading the carry in `spawnPlayer` would read the cleared copy and seed
nothing. The value the C# hands Kurt lives in the flow's fresh level result, so
`GameFlow` now exposes `levelHealth()` and the frontend seeds the **first** spawn from it;
a death respawn stays whole, because the C#'s second fresh Viewer finds the carry already
null (`Viewer.cs:347-361`). Pinned by two new rows in `flow_tests.cpp` — the carry arm
(40) and the no-carry arm (100), the latter because a default of 0 would otherwise read as a
passing default and kill Kurt on the first step.

**F4 (Low) — FIXED (prose).** The spawn comment said the DTI start position was "dropped 3
units onto the floor"; the code correctly *adds* 3 (`Viewer.cs:220`,
`StartPosition + (0,0,StartDrop)`). Reworded in `main_3ds.cpp`, and the same inverted prose
in `mdk_linux/src/main.cpp:333` was fixed in the same pass, since a reader who trusted it
would "fix" the code to `− 3.0f` and spawn Kurt inside the floor.

**F5 (Low) — FIXED (prose).** `mdk_3ds/src/platform/input_3ds.h` still described Start as
quit "until the flow is wired". The flow is wired; the table now says Start →
`flow::Event::Quit` → `Screen::None` ends the run because the menu Escape opens is cut, and
that Select is this frontend's second way out for the same reason, not a pending item.

**F2 (Medium) — ACCEPTED, docs.** `docs/CONTINUATION.md` priority-order item 5 is split
into **5a DONE** (flow → Player → FollowCamera → Kurt's sprite) and **5b OPEN — the HUD**,
blocked on the named cause (`mdk_render_canvas_quad` is a no-op on this backend, so a HUD
call would draw nothing while reading as a ported HUD). Item 8 (the red clear) is now
labelled builder-added and awaiting an owner line, since it is an addition to the owner's
order rather than a line in it.

### Rebutted, with evidence

**F1's "sharp detail" is wrong, and the spawn pin stays.** The review asserted that the
spawn pin's stated justification "does not hold — `bottom()` already includes any arena
containing his feet (`arena_space.cpp:160`), [so] the pin's only live effect is to *remove*
the by-bounds fallback from `move()`/`kurts()`". The first half is right and the
conclusion is not. `bottom()` takes the minimum over `{pinned} ∪ {arenas containing the
feet}`. When Kurt is below the world the second set is **empty**, so with no pin at all
`bottom()` returns false, `player.cpp:716` never fires, and he falls forever instead of
dying. Measured on level 7 in the new `vm_tests` case: pinned, `bottom(0,4,−1000)` answers
true with −39; unpinned, the same query answers false. The pin is load-bearing for the
fall-out death, so it is kept, and `arena_space.h` now says what it is actually for instead
of the claim the reviewer correctly attacked.

## Iteration 103 — batch 75: the red clear was a byte order, not a colour (owner item 8)

**What was implemented.** The Citro3D backend passed the frame's clear colour
straight to `C3D_RenderTargetClear`. The two ends of that seam pack a colour
differently and nothing in the signature says so: `MdkFrameParams::clear_colour`
is `0xAARRGGBB` — the seam's convention, which the Vulkan backend unpacks that
way (`mdk_linux/src/render/vk/vk_context.cpp:755`: R is `(clearColour >> 16) &
0xFF`) — while the PICA's clear word is `0xRRGGBBAA`, red in the TOP byte. The
pass-through therefore painted every frame with the **alpha byte as red**.

The conversion is `mdk::pica::clearColour()`, in `mdk_3ds/src/render/
pica_matrix.{h,cpp}` — the host-testable module for exactly this class of PICA
conversion, so the byte order is pinned by a host test and not only by a source
shape. `renderer_c3d.cpp` now converts on the way to both eye clears, and
`render.h` states the seam's byte order where a future backend will read it.

**This is the whole of "the red clear", and it was never a render-path failure.**
Owner item 8 was written as "blocked on the render path, named suspects: AGENTS
P2's GPU-state list and the depth map". Neither is implicated: the state and the
map are written every frame and the guest log still prints
`map z*1.0+1.0 near=0.0000 far=1.0000 clear=0xffffff test=LEQUAL` unchanged. The
clear was the wrong colour because it was the wrong order.

**Evidence — measured on the pinned instrument, before and after one rebuild.**
Mandarine r1.2.1 (`md5 0d2adab6`), `DISPLAY=:99`, capture by
`ffmpeg -f x11grab` (P7: the display, never the operator's screen; P8: the
pinned build). The panel's dominant colour, pixel counts over the full 1280x1024:

| build | panel clear | px |
|---|---|---|
| before | `#ff1020` (saturated red) | 58547 |
| after | `#102030` — exactly what `main_3ds.cpp:495` asked for | 58522 |

The geometry colours moved with it (`#ff287f`→`#e12a81`, `#ff1634`→`#8f1e3b`),
which is the framebuffer alpha being correct rather than 0x30; the triangles are
now legible as separate faces instead of washed into the background. Final run:
`emurun.sh` **exit 0**, guest log ends at **frame 3180**, `flow: screen=4
level=7`, 60 fps, mono (`render_3d=0`), llvmpipe forced. Emulator-green is not
hardware-pass (AGENTS P8).

**A negative result that saves the next batch time.** The obvious suspect for the
remaining geometry problem was the spawn, and it is innocent: the guest logs
`spawn: feet=(0.0,4.0,12.0) yaw=90.0`, which looks like an uninitialised
default, but reading `MDK/TRAVERSE/LEVEL7/LEVEL7.DTI` block 0 directly gives
`pos=(0.0000,4.0000,9.0000) angle=90.0000` — the DTI really does say that, so
`Dti::parse` and the `+ StartDrop` are faithful. Do not "fix" the spawn. What is
still wrong is that Kurt falls to `feet=(0.0,4.0,0.0)` and stops while the level's
first vertex is `(11.0,438.0,25.0)`, so the follow camera films the level from
outside it and the frame is a fan of triangles off one point.

**How the test got written, since it is the interesting part.** The first draft
asserted the converted word as four *memory bytes* (`b[0]==0x10` …). It went red
on a fix the emulator had already confirmed good: on a little-endian machine the
byte at offset 0 is the LOW byte, which here is the alpha, so a byte-indexed
expectation encodes the opposite of what the hardware sees. The row now asserts
bit fields, and both the header and the test say why in words, because the same
trap will be re-stepped on. A second draft error — B and A swapped in the
sweeping 256-value loop — was caught the same way, by running it.

**Gates, verbatim.**
- `make -C tests/scripts` → `All cases match the oracle.` (after the two test
  drafts above were corrected; it had failed `pica_matrix:511-514` and
  `pica_matrix:549` first, and the implementation was right both times)
- `bash tools/check.sh` → `CHECK: ALL GATES PASSED` (`audit_c_with_classes` 0,
  `gates_vfp` 0 blockers, `audit_arm11_math` clean, `audit_r11_idiv` none,
  `gates_core_parity` both targets link, `gates_smdh` SKIP no .cia,
  `gates_frames` CONTRACT CLEAN, `gates_batch_integrity` PASS)
- `make -C mdk_3ds` → `LINK mdk.elf` / `3DSX mdk.3dsx`
- also by hand: `sh tests/scripts/c3d_frame_test.sh` → `PASS C3dFrame (26 checks,
  33 arms adjudicated red)`; `bash tools/runner/test_review_state.sh` →
  `REVIEW STATE: ALL CASES PASS`.

**New pins.** `pica_matrix_tests.cpp::testTheClearColourByteOrder` (the measured
before/after words, the seam default, a non-255 alpha, and a 256-value channel
sweep), and `c3d_frame_test.sh::clear-colour-is-converted-for-the-pica` with the
mutation arm `clear-colour-passed-through-to-the-pica`, which is the tidy-up a
future builder is most likely to make — delete the "pointless" conversion — and
which no other gate can see, because `renderer_c3d.cpp` does not compile here.

## Iteration 104 — batch 76: the level-7 start lands on a floor, and the oracle lands him there too

**What was implemented.** No behaviour changed. This batch answers the question
`docs/CONTINUATION.md` handed it, with the oracle rather than with reasoning, and
pins the answer so the next batch cannot re-ask it.

Batch 75 read the Mandarine capture as "the follow camera films the level from
outside it": the guest log ended with Kurt at `feet=(0.0,4.0,0.0)` while "the
level's first vertex is `(11.0,438.0,25.0)`", and asked **why Kurt falls to z=0
and stops there instead of landing on a floor**. He is on a floor. The first
vertex of an arena's vertex list says nothing about where the start is. DANT_1
spans `(-172,-17,-27)..(263,1188,279)`, the start is inside it, and a BSP ray
down from the spawn hits a floor at **z = 0.01**. Measured with rays from
`(0,4,1)` through the pinned DANT_1:

```
  -X hits at (-25.10,4.00,1.00)   +X hits at (25.10,4.00,1.00)
  -Y hits at (0.00,-16.74,1.00)   +Y hits at (0.00,36.89,1.00)
  +Z hits nothing within 4000     -Z hits at (0.00,4.00,0.01)
  DANT_1 vertices=503, 24 within 50 of the spawn, 169 within 200
```

Kurt is standing in a room with walls at x = ±25.1, y = −16.74 and y = 36.89, a
floor at z = 0 and no ceiling. The follow camera's eye is `(0,-4,4.5)`, which is
*between* the two Y walls: the camera is inside the room, not outside the level.

**The oracle agrees exactly.** A `fall` mode was added to the headless C# probe
(`/tmp/mdk-pi/obj3/Probe`, scratch only): the level's own start dropped by
`StartDrop` as `Viewer.cs:220` does, stepped at `Viewer.Step` with nothing held,
in the C#'s own order (`kurt.Update`, `scripts.Update`, `space.SetSolid`). Its
output is now `tests/scripts/golden/L7_spawn_fall.txt`, and `tick1`'s new
`dump fall` is the C++ twin. The two are **byte-identical**, 61 lines:

```
level=7 start=0.0000,4.0000,9.0000 angle=90.0000 startArena=DANT_1

s=36 feet=0.0000,4.0000,0.1602 state=Fall floor=0 vert=-38.3995 bottom=-27.0000
```

## Iteration 106 — batch 78: the level-7 fan is not the cull, not the depth, and not the queue

**What was implemented.** No behaviour changed, and the fan is not fixed. This
batch answers the question `docs/CONTINUATION.md` handed it — "sample triangles
near the spawn and compare the vertices/MVP/clip values with host-derived
geometry; inspect the PICA winding and depth/cull behavior before modifying
renderer state" — and it answers it by measurement, which retires four
candidate causes at once and leaves one narrowed question.

Three code changes shipped, all of them instruments or real defects, none of them
a guess at the fan:

1. **A one-frame geometry census** (`Census`, `kCensusFrame = 120`,
   `renderer_c3d.cpp`). Batch 77 traced the first triangle of the first draw;
   that triangle is 442 units away and says nothing about the room the camera is
   standing in. The census walks every triangle the frame queues, in the same
   per-draw matrix the GPU is about to receive, and sorts it: behind the camera,
   outside the clip square, or on screen — and for the on-screen ones, which way
   they wind, how much screen area they claim, and where their bounding box
   reaches. It is cold by construction: `active` is true for exactly one frame of
   the process, so every other frame pays one integer compare.
2. **The per-draw log printed the wrong vertex.** `draw %d: ... v0=` read
   `mesh.data[0..2]` for every draw of a mesh, so all three logged draws showed
   `(11.0,438.0,25.0)` and batch 77 went looking for a fan in a triangle its draw
   did not contain. It now reads the draw's own `first_vertex`, and logs the pass.
3. **The diagnostic triangle's vertices were not in linear memory.** They were a
   `static float triangle[15]`, i.e. a `.bss` address in the application heap;
   citro3d hands that address to the GPU and nothing flushes the CPU cache for
   it. They now live in the renderer's `linearAlloc`'d scratch. **This is correct
   on its own terms and it is not sufficient** — see the measurement below.

### The census, from the actual build on the pinned emulator

```
census frame=120 draws=136 tris=852 behind=14 offscreen=13 onscreen=825
       near60=32 cw=544 ccw=281 w=[-13.0,1192.0] areaset=33.2835
census nearest draw=132 first=6 w=6.0 area=-0.03045586
       v0=(-0.312,2.000,1.500) v1=(0.936,2.000,1.500) v2=(0.936,2.000,0.741)
census ndc box=[-0.870,2.133]x[-2.408,2.408]
```

`view: 135 batches, 2544 vertices, 870 triangles` is the level build; the frame
queues 136 draws and 852 triangles and **825 of them land inside the clip
square**. So "the room is not queued" is false. `areaset=33.28` against a clip
square of area 4 is eight screens' worth of triangle area, so "the triangles are
thin slivers" is false too. The panel, measured by histogram off the capture, is
67.7% clear colour and 32% painted.

### Four causes measured and ruled out

* **The cull enum.** Forcing `GPU_CULL_NONE` on every pass changed the panel by
  **13 px of 96000**. The 281 counter-clockwise triangles contribute nothing
  either way, so the enum is not what is hiding the room. (This also settles the
  direction of the PICA's winding for the record: `GPU_CULL_BACK_CCW` discards
  the faces that look counter-clockwise on the panel, measured by drawing a
  known-wound triangle both ways.)
* **The depth test.** Forcing `test = false` on the Solid pass changed the panel
  by **58 px of 96000**. The depth map/test/clear triple is not rejecting the
  near geometry.
* **A sheared display transfer.** The target is 240x400 and the top screen's
  framebuffer is 400x240, so a `GX_TRANSFER_SCALE_NO` raw copy would shear. It
  does not: un-shearing the capture back through `src(x,y) = panel((y*240+x)%400,
  (y*240+x)/400)` produces a comb pattern, not a corridor, so the panel is not a
  raw copy of a coherent portrait image.
* **The portrait target itself.** Swapping to a 400x240 target and deleting the
  90-degree rotation from `pica::eyeViewProjection` was tried and **made it
  worse**: the panel went black apart from a 407x9 strip of clear colour, while
  the portrait configuration at least fills the panel with the clear colour. The
  rotation and the portrait target are the configuration that displays; a
  landscape target needs more than swapping the two constants, and both edits
  were reverted before this batch committed.

### What is left, and it is narrower than a fan

Replacing the scene's combiner source with `GPU_PRIMARY_COLOR` (so every
fragment is white and no texture is consulted) paints **exactly half the panel**:
47845 white px against 48155 clear px, split by a straight vertical edge at the
panel's centre. So the geometry that reaches the rasterizer covers half the view
and nothing covers the other half, and the split is a straight line through the
middle rather than a silhouette. With the texture back in, coverage drops from
50% to 32%, so the texture path discards a further ~18% of what the geometry
does paint.

Two questions follow, and they are different questions from "why a fan":

1. Why does the geometry stop at a straight line through the centre of the view?
   In the rotated portrait target that line is one NDC axis at 0, which is one
   camera axis at the eye — so either the projection's rotated axes put half the
   frustum outside the target, or the level's visible geometry really is one-sided
   from this camera. The oracle says the latter is false: `--frames=…,30,6` on
   the C# `mdk_sdl` at level 7, run after the landing (step 174), shows a
   symmetric corridor — bright floor across the bottom third, walls converging to
   a vanishing point at the centre, a dark ceiling band above it. The oracle's
   frame is the reference the next batch should diff against; it is at
   `/tmp/kilo-pi/orcframes/frame029.bmp` for this run and reproducible with the
   driver written to `/tmp/kilo-pi/orc_frames.sh`.
2. Why does the texture path discard ~18% of what is painted? That is the
   index-0-transparent palette expansion meeting a PICA path with no
   `C3D_AlphaTest` call of its own, and it is the same alpha source owner item 7
   names as blocked.

**The diagnostic triangle still does not appear, and that is measured too.** With
its vertices in linear memory, its winding tried both ways, the cull mode
`GPU_CULL_NONE`, the depth test off and vertices covering the whole clip square,
the panel did not change by a single pixel — while the scene, drawn with the same
program, the same attributes and the same viewport, paints half of it. The
linear-memory change is kept because a `.bss` pointer is not a GPU address, not
because it made the triangle appear. Whatever else is wrong with that draw is
still open, and it is a diagnostic, not the game.

**Review-4 findings.** All four are Medium and none is claimed fixed. F1 (the
geometric solid-arena re-pin) and F2 (the placed-fall golden) stay deferred to a
collision batch, unchanged from batch 77's disposition. F3 (the frame gate
accepts a duplicate capture) and F4 (the worktree's routing versus the committed
owner directive, and the two `100755 => 100644` mode changes) remain owner
actions on owner-protected paths; nothing under `ralph/`, `ralph-pi.sh` or
`tools/runner/test_review_state.sh` was staged here, and `MDK_OWNER_APPROVED` was
not set. This batch's pinned pair is again the level-3 Linux frame, for the same
reason F3 states: the level-3 host frame's path did not change. The 3DS evidence
is the emulator verdict and the census above, and the sidecar says so.

## Iteration 107 — batch 79: the audio sample plane is ported, and it is bit-for-bit the C# mixer

**What this batch is.** Owner-directive item 6's first half: `sound_device.h:13`
used to say the sample plane "belongs to the platform backends and is not ported
yet". It is now ported, and it is ported **in `mdk_core`**, not in a backend, for
the reason the whole port runs on: the C# mixes in software, the C# is the oracle,
and a mix that lives behind a platform seam cannot be pinned against it. The
backends keep exactly one decision — what happens to the finished buffer — through
a `Sink` function pointer plus a context (AGENTS.md 10 refuses `std::function`),
and a NULL sink is the oracle's own `Output.Muted`: mixed and dropped.

| New / changed | Oracle | What landed |
|---|---|---|
| `mdk_core/src/audio/sound.{h,cpp}` | `AudioDevice.cs`'s `Sound` + `Sound.FromPcm` | both PCM widths, the two scale constants, the `data.Length & ~1` odd-byte drop, `Frames` |
| `mdk_core/src/audio/limiter.{h,cpp}` | `Limiter.cs` | one gain for both channels, the ceiling/release constants cached in the constructor, the stateful `_gain` decay across frames |
| `mdk_core/src/audio/sound_device.{h,cpp}` | `AudioDevice.Update/AddMusic/MixVoice/Sample`, `MasterGain`, `SetBusGain`, `MusicFilter` | the mix and music buffers, the interpolation, the DirectSound pan law, the one-pole music low-pass, the bus/master volumes, the limiter, the sink seam |
| `mdk_core/src/audio/sound_bank.{h,cpp}` | `SoundBank.Load` → `Sound.FromPcm` | the bank now decodes and owns the samples; `Entry.sound` points at the bank's one decode per name (the sharing the C# gets from `Sound` being a reference type); copy/move deleted |
| `tests/scripts/tick1.cpp` | — | `mix` / `mixmeta` drivers moved into `audioMixDump` / `audioMetaDump` and wired to two new goldens |

**The goldens are the oracle's output, not the port's.** The scratch driver
`/tmp/mdk-pi/obj3/MixProbe` (new, scratch-only, never committed) calls the **real**
`SoundBank` and the **real** `AudioDevice`; the frames owed and the mix buffer come
out of the device's own private `_owed` / `_mix` by reflection, so the harness adds
no arithmetic of its own. Before believing it, the scratch tree was checked against
the read-only repository oracle: `AudioDevice.cs`, `Limiter.cs`, `SoundBank.cs`,
`SoundMixer.cs`, `Wav.cs`, `Sni.cs` all `cmp`-identical.

- `golden/L3_audio_mix.txt` (41 lines, sha256 `2ded2f07…`) — 40 updates of an
  eight-voice schedule chosen to cover both PCM widths (FOOT1 16-bit, EXPLODE
  8-bit), both buses, both loop states, a `Set` on a live voice, a `Stop`, a
  `StopAll`, pans at each extreme and past it, pitches away from 1, and enough
  level to drive the limiter. Each line is `sum` (double accumulator), `min`/`max`
  and the first/last four samples, all as **bit patterns**.
  `cmp /tmp/mdk-pi/b79_oracle_mix.txt tests/scripts/golden/L3_audio_mix.txt` →
  **identical**, and the C++ `tick1 mix 3 40` is identical to both.
- `golden/L3_audio_meta.txt` (9 lines, sha256 `5247a4cb…`) — the same eight sounds
  decoded: length, rate, loop flag and four sample bit patterns each. Also
  **identical** on both sides, which is what makes a future mix divergence
  localisable to the mixer rather than the decode.
- The limiter is not a bystander in this golden: `max=3F71ADF9` appears on the
  updates where the mix is hot, which is the ceiling itself, so the clamp is live
  and equal on both sides.

**Constants measured, not asserted.** The port caches four constants the C#
computes with `MathF`; a comment claiming a bit pattern is only worth its
verification. `mdkmix 3 1 bits` (the oracle's own `MathF.Pow`/`MathF.Exp`) against
a host C program: `far(pan 0.5)=3B4F3E37`, `ceiling=3F71ADF9`, `release=396DC000`,
`music alpha=3F131C9A` — **all four identical**, and `3.14159265f` is the same
float as `MathF.PI`.

**One estimate was wrong and is now a measurement.** The draft comments said
decoding a level "doubles" its WAV to "~9 MB". Counted through the oracle: level
3's three archives are 4,390,060 bytes and hold **72 sounds = 3,234,976 samples =
12.34 MB of float**, because MDK's sounds are mostly 8-bit and a float is four
bytes. Against a 16 MB FCRAM that is not a rounding error, so `sound.h` and
`sound_bank.h` now carry the measured number and the consequence: the ndsp batch
cannot preload the bank on the console. Nothing calls `preload()` on the 3DS today
(`main_3ds.cpp` builds no bank); `mdk_linux/src/main.cpp:239` does, which is what
the C# `Viewer` does too.

**Hot path, and said plainly.** A voice's mix loop runs 735 iterations a frame, and
AGENTS.md 2's **second** criterion makes anything at 256+ a frame hot path with no
capture at all — the empty corpus waives the staleness clocks, not the
classification. The draft header claimed "no pin is due" while the files carried
pins, which is both wrong and the kind of thing §5 exists to prevent. The header
now argues the classification, and `mixVoice`'s frame loop carries an
`@vfp-exempt R2,R3,R4` pin for the double position, the wrap compare and the
`(int)` index together, because those three choose which two samples every output
frame interpolates between, i.e. the samples the golden pins. `measured n/a`
because there is no OG capture to measure against. `gates_vfp` still reports
`PASS blockers=0`.

**What is NOT done, stated as not done.** No shipped frontend calls
`SoundDevice::update()` yet, so no sample reaches a speaker on either target from
this batch: the SDL sink (Linux) and the ndsp sink (3DS) are the second half of
item 6. The mix is real and pinned; the plumbing that would hear it is not written.
Streamed voices (`PlayStream`/`Push`) stay unported — nothing in the scripts uses
them. `Record` (the C#'s WAV capture) is not ported: the probe digests the buffer
directly, so the golden does not need it.

## Iteration 108 — batch 80: the game is audible on both targets, and the ndsp path is measured

**What landed.** The mix was ported and pinned in batch 79 and nothing could hear
it: no shipped frontend called `SoundDevice::update()`, and neither target had a
sink. This batch is the plumbing, and it is the last audio item on the owner's
priority order before the console can be said to *play* rather than simulate.

1. **The sink seam grew its second half** (`mdk_core/src/audio/sound_device.{h,cpp}`).
   The C#'s `Update` has two answers for how many frames to mix and picks by
   whether it has a stream (`AudioDevice.cs:217-221`):

   ```csharp
   var frames = _stream == null ? (int)_owed
       : (int)(OutputRate * QueueSeconds) - SDL_GetAudioStreamQueued(_stream) / bytesPerFrame;
   _owed -= _stream == null ? frames : _owed;
   ```

   A one-way push seam cannot express that, so `setSink` now takes an optional
   `queued` query alongside the `write` hook. A sink that can answer it (SDL — it
   is the same SDL call the C# makes) gets the top-up branch; a sink that cannot
   keeps the `owed += rate*delta` accounting, which is the muted device's and the
   one `golden/L3_audio_mix.txt` pins. Both branches are the oracle's line for
   line; what moved is which sink is allowed to take which.
2. **`mdk_linux/src/audio/audio_sdl.{h,cpp}`** — the output half of
   `AudioDevice.cs`: `SDL_InitSubSystem(AUDIO)`, `SDL_OpenAudioDeviceStream` with
   `SDL_AUDIO_F32LE` stereo 44100 (SPEC.md §8's "1:1 with the C#"),
   `SDL_ResumeAudioStreamDevice`, `SDL_PutAudioStreamData`,
   `SDL_GetAudioStreamQueued`, `SDL_DestroyAudioStream`. No device is not an
   error: the C# falls back to muted and so does this, which is why the capture
   path is untouched.
3. **`mdk_3ds/src/audio/audio_3ds.{h,cpp}`** — the ndsp sink. ONE channel (0),
   `NDSP_FORMAT_STEREO_PCM16` at 44100, four 20 ms wave buffers in one
   `linearAlloc` (14,112 bytes), float→PCM16 converted here (SPEC.md §8 puts the
   conversion at the sink so the mix stays the shared float one), `DSP_FlushDataCache`
   before each `ndspChnWaveBufAdd`, a DONE-poll reap of our own (ndsp exposes no
   play position), a drop-not-block policy when every buffer is still in the DSP's
   hands, and a **clear + reset + re-configure before the first buffer after a
   drain** — the drained channel does not wake on a new buffer, the same trap the
   vault's Forsaken audio finding records for its music queue
   (`10-projects/forsaken/findings/dsp-adpcm-music-and-sfx-audio.md` §A).
   **There is deliberately no audio worker thread**: the sink has nothing to read,
   so there is no blocking work to hide from the frame, and a worker would have
   carried R1's second FPSCR state and §10's small-stack rule for nothing. R1's
   audio row is satisfied by `vfpThreadFzDn()` at the audio subsystem's entry with
   its read-back logged, and the call is documented as defensive (the frame's
   thread is main, which set FZ|DN before `gfxInitDefault`).
4. **Both frontends hear the game.** Linux: `audioOpen()`, `player.setMixer(&runtime->mixer())`,
   and per frame `listenFromCamera` → `mixer.update(elapsed)` → `device().update(elapsed)`,
   in the C#'s two places (Viewer.cs:686-696 then Game.cs:334-337). 3DS: the
   level's SNI archives load, a standalone `SoundMixer` (this frontend has no
   `ScriptRuntime` yet) gets the Player, the ndsp sink is set, and the same three
   calls run per frame. `SoundMixer::listenFromCamera` derives the eye's right as
   `Cross(Forward, Up)` — FollowCamera.cs:201's own expression and the same vector
   `camera_builder.cpp` builds the view matrix from, so it is the oracle's basis
   restated rather than a second convention; the scope-listening half stays
   deferred with Kurt's sniper, and `scopeZoom` therefore stays 0.
5. **The 3DS memory question, answered and named.** `bank.preload()` is NOT called
   on the console. Level 3 decodes to 12.34 MB of float, level 4 to 15.03 MB and
   level 8 to 19.08 MB (the batch-79 review counted all three) against 16 MB of
   FCRAM, so decoding the whole bank is impossible and was never attempted:
   `SoundBank::get` decodes on first use, so the console pays for what a level
   actually plays. That does not BOUND the total, and the follow-up is named in
   CONTINUATION rather than left implicit: an int16 sample store would halve all
   three numbers with no change to a single sample value (both PCM scales are
   powers of two, so `(byte-128)*256 * (1/32768)` is the same float as
   `(byte-128)*(1/128)`), and a budget-and-evict is the alternative.

**New checks.** `tests/scripts/audio_sink_tests.{h,cpp}` — `PASS AudioSinkSeam`,
TRANSLITERATED (cited to the lines above; the queue branch cannot be *measured*
here because the scratch probe that produced the audio golden ran the muted
device and this host has no sound device). It pins 2646 as
`(int)(44100 * 0.06f)`, the top-up at 0/1000/2646/5000 queued frames, the
