## Iteration 109 — batch 81: the ndsp sink never queued anything, and now it does

**Review remediated:** `logs/ralph-pi/run-20261106-035708/review-1.md` (DeepSeek V4.1
Flash TH, independent, on batch 80's commit). Verdict was INCOMPLETE on F1 (High)
and F2/F3/F4 (Medium). Every finding is dispositioned below — and the investigation
F1 asked for found a **Critical defect the review could not see**, which is the
story of this batch.

### The defect: `ndspChnWaveBufAdd` refuses a buffer it thinks is already queued

Batch 80's `submit()` did `s.wave.status = NDSP_WBUF_QUEUED;` immediately before
`ndspChnWaveBufAdd(kChannel, &s.wave)`. Disassembly of
`/opt/devkitpro/libctru/lib/libctru.a:ndsp-channel.o` (r1 = the wavebuf, offset
17 = `status`):

```
ldrb ip, [r1, #17] ; sub ip, ip, #1 ; cmp ip, #1 ; bls <the epilogue at +0xb8>
mov  r3, #1 ; strb r3, [r1, #17] ; str r3, [r1, #20]   ; status = QUEUED, next = NULL
... append to the channel's wave-buffer list ...
```

> Corrected by Iteration 110 (review F4 of run-20261106-062909, re-verified here
> with a fresh `arm-none-eabi-objdump`): the branch at +0x54 targets +0xb8, which
> is `add sp, sp, #20 ; pop {lr} ; b LightLock_Unlock`. The sequence-id store
> (`strh r3, [r1, #18]`) is at +0xac, on the LINKING path only, so a QUEUED or
> PLAYING buffer gets no sequence id either. The conclusion and the fix are
> unchanged; the mechanism described below was wrong.

For `status` QUEUED(1) or PLAYING(2) it **returns without linking the buffer**;
it is libctru that sets QUEUED on the way in. So
pre-setting QUEUED made every submit a silent no-op. The DSP was handed nothing,
so nothing ever came back `DONE`, so `reap()` never freed a slot, so the queue
filled after four buffers and `audioSink` dropped **every** mix after the first
80 ms of the run.

Batch 80 reported success because its evidence was `sink=1` and `plays=1`.
`sink=1` means `ndspInit()` returned 0. `plays=1` counts launched mixer **voices**
(`device().nextId() - 1`) and has nothing to do with ndsp. Review F4 said exactly
that — "nothing in the log shows that one wave buffer was ever handed to ndsp" —
and it was right in the strongest possible way.

### F1 (High) — CONFIRMED, fixed, and settled by measurement, not by argument

The reviewer's reading is correct: `nsamples` for a stereo format is in **frames**.
The evidence is genuinely two-sided on paper — libctru's own header comment says
"PCM16=halfwords" and `examples/3ds/audio/ogg-vorbis-decoding` follows it — so
this was measured rather than argued. Four devkitPro examples that are
unambiguously stereo pass frames (`audio/streaming` and `audio/filters` pass
`SAMPLESPERBUF` against a 4-bytes-per-frame buffer, `audio/modplug-decoding`
passes `(decoded/2)/sizeof(int16_t)`, `audio/opus-decoding` passes `totalSamples`
counted in frames), and so does the hardware-proven `../forsaken/sound_3ds.c:467`
that the owner directive told this port to adapt.

The measurement is the sink's own counters (F4's instrument) against a production
rate that is real time by construction: one 735-frame mix per 60 Hz frame is
exactly 50 buffers of 882 frames a second. Three builds, same harness, same
pinned emulator, same level:

| build | submitted | done | dropped | inDsp | last frame |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `status=QUEUED`, `nsamples=1764` (batch 80) | 4 | 0 | 2579 | 4 | 2580 |
| `status=FREE`, `nsamples=1764` (halfwords) | 1030 | 1026 | 1435 | 4 | 2460 |
| `status=FREE`, `nsamples=882` (**this batch**) | 2156 | 2153 | 12 | 3 | 2580 |

Row 2 is the discriminator: the DSP retired 1030 buffers while the mix produced
~2050 — **exactly half**, i.e. it spent 40 ms on a buffer holding 20 ms of stereo,
which is what reading 1764 as 1764 frames does. Row 3 retires 2153 of 2156 with
`inDsp=3`, i.e. production and consumption are equal and the 12 drops are all in
the level-load stall. The halfwords reading was also a 3528-byte DSP read from a
3528-byte slot — and past the end of the 14,112-byte `linearAlloc` for the last
slot, as the review said.

Fix: `s.wave.nsamples = (u32)kBufFrames;`. The `DSP_FlushDataCache` length stays
`kBufHalfwords * sizeof(int16_t)` — it is a byte count and already correct.

**Still open, stated plainly:** this is the emulator's HLE DSP. The Old-3DS
firmware's behaviour is not measured (AGENTS P6/P8), and `libctru`'s header still
says halfwords. The counters are the instrument to read on hardware.

### F4 (Medium) — fixed: the sink is now observable

`mdk_3ds/src/audio/audio_3ds.h` gained `AudioStats` + `audioStats()`:
`submitted`, `done`, `dropped`, `requeued` (submits that had to re-configure a
drained channel), plus ndsp's own `ndspGetFrameCount()`/`ndspGetDroppedFrames()`,
and `main_3ds.cpp` logs the ledger every 60 frames. `submitted x 20 ms` is what
the mix produced and `done` is what the DSP returned, so a rate bug is a number
in the guest log instead of an inference. The final run reads
`submitted=2156 done=2153 dropped=12 requeued=1 inDsp=3 dspframes=8844` —
`submitted - done == inDsp`, so the ledger balances.

> Corrected by Iteration 110 (review F1): `done` cannot carry a rate test, because
> `submitted - done == inDsp <= 4` by construction. The sentence above is the
> reading this iteration had wrong; the rate lives in `submitted` against the
> frame, and the ledger line now prints the frame so it can be divided.

### F2 (Medium) — confirmed: the comment claimed a measurement that does not exist

`audio_3ds.h` said the 80 ms queue was "Measured against the level-3 load, not
guessed". No such measurement exists. The comment now says the doubling was a
design choice, names the only load number on disk (the emulator's 129.5 ms level-7
load frame = 6.5 buffers), and states the consequence the review drew: a frame
longer than the queue underruns it by construction, and no queue depth survives
that. The 12 drops in the fixed run are that statement, measured.

### F3 (Medium) — deferred to an owner decision, with the oracle's number recorded

`SPEC.md:809` asks for a 24-voice pool and a 40 ms queue on the 3DS; the port
ships 64 and 80. This is not the builder's to resolve: SPEC.md is owner-protected
(it cannot be amended here), and the oracle has `MaxVoices = 64`
(`src/Mdk.Engine/Audio/AudioDevice.cs:73`) with **no platform branch**, so
implementing 24 would deviate from the oracle in the opposite direction. The
conflict is recorded as an owner action in `docs/CONTINUATION.md` with both
readings, and `audio_3ds.h` no longer asserts its own reading as fact. The cost
argument stays unmeasured (the hot-path corpus is empty) and nothing in the current
build exceeds a handful of voices.

### F5 (Low) — fixed: the number in the comment is now the one the code produces

`tests/scripts/audio_sink_tests.cpp` said "44100 * (1/60) is
735.00000000000007 in double". Neither half was true: `44100 * (1.0/60.0)` is
exactly `735.0`, and the code's `delta` is a float, so
`(double)44100 * (double)delta` is `735.0000383332372`. The comment now carries
the real value and says why the pure-double one is not what the branch computes.

### F6 (Low) — fixed

`docs/CONTINUATION.md` cited "Owner item 7" for Citro3D alpha blend; the owner
directive numbers it 6. Both the priority-order row and the NEXT section now cite
the directive's number and say the file's own numbering drifted.

### The pin: `tests/scripts/ndsp_sink_test.sh`

`renderer_c3d.cpp` already has a source-shape gate for the same reason — a 3DS
backend that includes `<3ds.h>` cannot be compiled on a host, so nothing else in
`make -C tests/scripts` can reach it. `ndsp_sink_test.sh` does the same job for
the sink: 11 checks (status FREE before the add, QUEUED/PLAYING never pre-set,
`nsamples` from `kBufFrames`, the flush still in bytes, the counters present, the
frontend publishing the ledger) with 6 mutation arms, each of which must turn a
named check red. `PASS NdspSink (11 checks, 6 arms adjudicated red)`, wired into
`tests/scripts/Makefile` after `c3d_frame_test.sh`.

### Gates, as run

* `make -C tests/scripts` → **`All cases match the oracle.`** including
  `PASS L3_audio_mix`, `PASS L3_audio_meta`, and the new
  `PASS NdspSink (11 checks, 6 arms adjudicated red)` alongside
  `PASS C3dFrame (26 checks, 33 arms)`, `PASS Main3dsFlow (5 checks, 5 arms)`,
  `PASS EmurunHarness (68 checks)`.
* `bash tools/check.sh` → **`CHECK: ALL GATES PASSED`**:
  `audit_c_with_classes 0 violations`, `gates_vfp 0 blockers`,
  `audit_arm11_math contract clean`, `audit_r11_idiv no candidates`,
  `gates_core_parity both targets link the same core`,
  `SKIP gates_smdh (no built .cia)`, `PASS gates_frames L3_f1.bmp
  sha=58615fc85d02e009`, `gates_batch_integrity project invariants intact`.
* `DEVKITPRO=/opt/devkitpro DEVKITARM=/opt/devkitpro/devkitARM make -C mdk_3ds`
  → **`3DSX mdk.3dsx`**.

### Emulator evidence (AGENTS P7/P8) — `mdk_3ds/tools/emurun.sh --min-frames 120`, exit 0

```
display   : :99
emulator  : mandarine.AppImage md5 0d2adab6   (r1.2.1, the pinned known good)
gl        : forced llvmpipe, graphics_api=1
stereo    : render_3d=0 factor_3d=0 (mono)
audio     : SDL_AUDIODRIVER=dummy ALSA_CARD=null AUDIODEV=null cfg volume=0
dspfirm   : dspfirm.cdc (the lane's sdmc/3ds/dspfirm.cdc; ndsp needs it)
captures  : /tmp/kilo-pi/emurun-b81.txt (the lane's own log dir is named in it)
guest log : audio: FZ/DN 1 (fpscr=83000010)
            audio: ndsp chn0 PCM16 stereo 44100 Hz, 4 x 20 ms queued
            audio: sink=1 bank=1 voices=0 queue=2646
            audio: submitted=2156 done=2153 dropped=12 requeued=1 inDsp=3 dspframes=8844
            frame 2580 elapsed=0.0167 steps=2592 ... voices=0 plays=1
```

`submitted=2156 done=2153` is the line that matters, and it is the first evidence
this project has ever produced that a wave buffer reached the DSP and came back.
`dspframes` advancing 8844 times says the DSP was mixing the whole run.
Emulator-green is not hardware-pass: the HLE DSP is not the firmware, the lane's

## Iteration 110 — batch 82: the sink's instrument could not detect the bug it was built for

**Review remediated:** `logs/ralph-pi/run-20261106-062909/review-1.md` (DeepSeek
V4.1 Flash TH, independent, on batch 81's commit `458f8d3`). Verdict INCOMPLETE
with **no Critical and no High**; the actionable residue was F1 (Medium), F2
(Medium, owner-only) and F3–F6 (Low). Every one was investigated against primary
evidence before anything was changed, and **all five code/test findings were
confirmed** — none is rebutted. F2 is an owner reconciliation, recorded not fixed.

### F1 (Medium) — CONFIRMED: the documented reading of the counters was impossible

The counters' comment said `done ~= submitted` means the DSP consumes at the
nameplate rate and `done ~= submitted/2` with `dropped ~= submitted/2` is what a
wrong `nsamples` unit looks like. The reviewer is right that that reading cannot
occur, and the arithmetic is short: `g_submitted++` and `g_inDsp++` execute
together in `submit()`, and `g_done++` and `g_inDsp--` execute together at **both**
retirement sites, so `submitted - done == inDsp` is an identity and `inDsp <=
kNumBufs == 4`. Therefore `done` is always within four of `submitted`. Checked
against batch 81's own three-row table:

| build | frames | submitted | expected (frames x 735/882) | ratio | done | done/submitted | dropped | inDsp |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `status=QUEUED` (batch 80) | 2580 | 4 | 2150 | **0.002** | 0 | — | 2579 | 4 |
| `nsamples=1764` (halfwords) | 2460 | 1030 | 2050 | **0.502** | 1026 | 0.996 | 1435 | 4 |
| `nsamples=882` (correct) | 2580 | 2156 | 2150 | **1.003** | 2153 | 0.999 | 12 | 3 |

`done/submitted` is ~1.0 in **every** row, including the two broken ones, so the
documented rule would have certified batch 80's broken sink as healthy — the exact
false pass the counters exist to prevent. The discriminator is `submitted` against
what the clock owes (the **ratio** column: 0.002 / 0.502 / 1.003), plus `inDsp`
pinned at 4 while `dropped` climbs (both broken rows), plus `requeued ~= submitted`
for the opposite failure, plus `dspframes` ~205 per 60 guest frames. `dropped`
counts **rejected fills**, not buffers — one increment discards up to a whole
frame's 735 samples, 0.83 of a buffer, which is why row 2 shows 1435 drops for
~1020 buffers' worth discarded.

Fixed in `audio_3ds.cpp`, `audio_3ds.h` and the gate's header: the four real
readings are stated with the measured value for each, and the impossible one is
named as impossible so nobody re-derives it. **The instrument was also made
self-reading**: the ledger line now prints `frame=` next to `submitted=`, because
the only discriminating ratio needs both numbers and they were on two different
log lines printed for two different reasons. Measured on this batch's run:
`audio: frame=2580 submitted=2156 done=2153 dropped=8 requeued=1 inDsp=3
dspframes=8844 dspdropped=0` → 2156/2150 = 1.003, `submitted - done == inDsp`,
`dspframes` 205.7 per 60 frames. All three discriminators now read off one line.

### F4 (Low) — CONFIRMED from a fresh disassembly, fixed in all three copies

Re-derived here rather than trusted: `arm-none-eabi-objdump -d` of
`/opt/devkitpro/libctru/lib/libctru.a:ndsp-channel.o` gives `+0x54: bls +0xb8`,
and `+0xb8` is `add sp, sp, #20 ; pop {lr} ; b LightLock_Unlock` — the epilogue.
The sequence-id store `strh r3, [r1, #18]` is at `+0xac`, reachable only by falling
through from `+0x58` on the **linking** path. So a QUEUED/PLAYING buffer is not
merely unlinked, it gets no sequence id either. The prose in `audio_3ds.cpp`,
`ndsp_sink_test.sh` and Iteration 109 said "assigns a sequence id and returns";
all three now carry the addresses and the correct mechanism, and Iteration 109
carries a marked correction rather than a silent rewrite. The `status = FREE` fix
itself is unaffected — the reviewer attacked it and could not break it either.

### F5 (Low) — CONFIRMED by reproducing the mutation, fixed with four checks and four arms

The reviewer deleted the **second** `g_done++` (the one in `audioSink`'s re-check,
whose own comment says it exists so the ledger does not under-report) and the gate
still passed. Reproduced here: `rc=0`, `PASS NdspSink (11 checks, 6 arms)`. The
gate only looked inside `reap()`'s body. `ndsp_sink_test.sh` now has **15 checks
and 10 arms**, adding `counts-done-at-the-sink-recheck`, `ledger-balances` (each
retirement site pairs `g_done++` with `g_inDsp--`, and `g_inDsp++` sits with
`g_submitted++` — that pairing is what makes the ledger a proof), `counts-requeued`
and `frontend-logs-the-frame-with-the-ledger`. Re-running the reviewer's exact
mutation now gives `rc=1` with
`FAIL ndsp_sink counts-done-at-the-sink-recheck`. All 10 arms adjudicate red, and
each new arm targets the second site by its own text (`slot.` vs `s.`) so it cannot
collide with `reap()`'s identical statement.

## Iteration 111 — batch 83: the opaque passes were blending, and the discard the shader had was never ported

**Owner directive item 6** ("Citro3D alpha blend"), and the last unimplemented
half of the `Pass` state table. One subsystem: the alpha state of a pass — its
blend factors and the discard that stands in for the shader's `discard`.

### The named blocker was wrong in both directions, and the measurement is the batch

`docs/OPEN_ITEMS.md` said the blend half could not land because "there is no
alpha to blend with on this path" and "the PICA has no discard", and that glass
therefore "draws opaque" because `C3D_AlphaBlend` is never called. Both halves
came apart under measurement, and the direction they came apart in is the whole
batch.

**1. citro3d's own initialiser had been blending every frame since the port began.**
Read out of the archive this project links, not out of a document —
`arm-none-eabi-objdump -d` over `libcitro3dd.a:base.o`, `C3D_Init`:

```
 f8:  bl C3D_AlphaTest      ; r0=0 (false), r1=1 (GPU_ALWAYS), r2=0
114:  bl C3D_AlphaBlend     ; r0=0 r1=0 (ADD,ADD) r2=6 (SRC_ALPHA)
                            ; r3=7 (ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA) [sp]=6 [sp+4]=7
```

So blending was **on** for every pass of every frame, with the oracle's *colour*
pair and not its alpha pair. That is why glass looked plausible and why "glass is
opaque" was never the symptom. What the port actually had was the opposite
defect: the four passes the oracle marks `enable_blend = false` were mixing.

**2. The oracle's alpha source is already on this path, and the PICA does have a
discard.** `shaders/palette.hlsl` has two branches. Flat colour:
`return colour * input.colour` — the material's alpha (the DTI's glass alpha)
reaches the fragment, and this backend carries it: `flatColourId` packs the
alpha into the 1x1 texture and `expandRgba` copies all four bytes. Textured:
`float4(palette.rgb, 1.0) * colour * input.colour` preceded by
`if (index == 0) discard;`. The PICA's equivalent of that discard is the alpha
test, and the expansion this backend already does makes it exact: `expandIndices`
leaves index 0 as RGBA(0,0,0,0) and forces alpha 255 on every other index, so
`alpha > 0` selects precisely the texels the shader keeps.

**3. And the discard is not cosmetic, which is the reason it was worth a batch.**
A fragment blended with alpha 0 still **writes depth**; a discarded fragment does
not. Until this batch every transparent texel of every arena texture painted a
hole in the depth buffer that hid whatever was behind it — an invisible wall in
the game's own colours.

### What was implemented

- `mdk_3ds/src/render/pica_matrix.{h,cpp}` — `BlendState` + `BlendFactor` and
  `blendStateForPass(Pass, Blend)`, the oracle's block (`Renderer.cs:565-576`)
  spelled out factor by factor, in host-readable ints because this file compiles
  on the host. Plus `kAlphaTestReference` and `alphaTestPasses(int)`, the shader's
  discard as a predicate a test can hold.
- `mdk_3ds/src/render/renderer_c3d.cpp` — `gpuBlendFactor`, `installBlendState`,
  a two-int cache beside the cull and depth caches, the per-draw install on a
  pass/blend transition, and in `installEye` the frame's `C3D_AlphaTest(true,
  GPU_GREATER, 0)` plus the default (Solid) blend state. AGENTS P2 is the rule
  this satisfies: all GPU state is written explicitly every frame, and a register
  whose value comes from a library's initialiser is not written by this backend.
- `tests/scripts/pica_matrix_tests.cpp` — four new cases: the opaque passes
  replace on **both** channels, the blended pass uses the oracle's factors and
  its alpha pair differs from its colour pair, `Add` moves only the destination
  colour, and the discard is `alpha > 0` (so a half-transparent glass alpha
  survives it).

Verified in the linked object, not assumed: `objdump` of `build/renderer_c3d.o`
shows `mov r2,#0; mov r1,#6; mov r0,#1; bl C3D_AlphaTest` — `(true, GPU_GREATER,
0)` — and one `C3D_AlphaBlend` call site in `installBlendState`.

### Emulator evidence (AGENTS P7/P8)

`DISPLAY=:99`, `mdk_3ds/tools/emurun.sh --secs 30 --shot ...`, pinned Mandarine
`md5 0d2adab6` (r1.2.1, the known-good; r1.3.0 was not used), exit code **0**
both runs, fresh lane per run, guest log read from the lane. Before: log ends at
frame 2220. After: log ends at frame 1680. Both `backend: PICA200 Citro3D`,
`flow: screen=4 level=7`, 60 FPS, mono, dummy audio. Display recorded: **:99**.
Captures under `/tmp/mdk-b83/` (`/tmp/kilo` is not writable by this uid).

The picture moved, and it moved in exactly the direction the oracle predicts:

| measure (400x240 top panel, 95361 px) | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| pixels within tolerance 16 of the clear colour | 68001 (71.3%) | 58127 (61.0%) |
| differing pixels, whole capture | — | 33909 of 1310720 (2.59%) |
| of the changed pixels | — | 33844 brighter, **65 darker** |

The change is confined to `x 640..839, y 253..752` — the drawn half of the panel.
The top transitions are `(225,42,129)→(255,44,141)`, `(143,30,59)→(255,28,69)`,
`(30,30,45)→(255,0,0)`. That last one is the arithmetic of the bug: a surface the
palette says is pure red was landing at `(30,30,45)`, which is
`src*(16/255) + clear*(1-16/255)` — an opaque arena surface drawn at six percent
over the background. After the fix it is the palette's own colour.

**What the capture does NOT show, stated plainly.** The near-clear count improved
by 9874 px because geometry that was already being drawn stopped being drawn
nearly transparent; no geometry appeared that had been depth-hidden, so the
alpha test's depth-write consequence is not visible in this scene and the
one-sided view — geometry still stops at column 640 of 839 — is **still open**.
The two changes are one batch and the capture cannot attribute between them.
Emulator-green is not hardware-pass: llvmpipe is not the PICA, and a register
pair this emulator accepts may still differ on a console (AGENTS P8).

### Review findings from `logs/ralph-pi/run-20261106-062909/review-2.md`

No Critical and no High, so nothing was mandatory. Dispositions:

- **F1 (Medium) — CONFIRMED, record corrected.** The reviewer is right that
  Iteration 110's "nothing is added after frame 60" is falsified by its own
  capture, and it is corrected in place there rather than left to propagate: the
  drops run 3 → 5 → 6 → 7 → 8 across frames 60 → 1440. Whether the five late
  rejects are HLE jitter or a real underrun stays open and needs an OG run.
- **F2 (Medium) — CONFIRMED, deferred with cause.** `dspframes` is in DSP sound
  frames at `NDSP_SAMPLE_RATE = SYSCLOCK_SOC/512 = 32728.5 Hz`, ~204.5/s, not
  "240-sample blocks at 48 kHz"; the comment in `audio_3ds.{h,cpp}` says the
  wrong unit. Deferred because it is the audio subsystem and this batch's slice
  is the renderer's alpha state; the corrected text is recorded here so the next
  audio-docs batch is mechanical. Filed in `docs/CONTINUATION.md` as the next
  small batch.
- **F3 (Medium) — CONFIRMED, deferred with cause.** The `frames × 735/882`
  denominator is exact only at 60 fps, because `elapsedFor(false, step, delta)`
  returns the wall delta; at 30 fps a half-rate sink would read "matched". The
  fix is to state the fps precondition beside the denominator (or make the test
  wall-clock based). Same audio-docs batch.
- **F4 (Medium) — CONFIRMED, deferred with cause.** `inDsp` pinned at 4 is also
  the signature of "nothing was ever submitted", so the reading must be qualified
  with `submitted > 0`. Same audio-docs batch.
- **F5 (Low) — CONFIRMED, deferred with cause.** `submitted - done == inDsp`
  holds for an **open** sink; `audioClose()` zeroes `g_inDsp` and not the other
  two. One-word prose fix, same batch.
- **F6 (Low) — OWNER ONLY, untouched.** Every file it names
  (`docs/OWNER_DIRECTIVE_2026-11-05.md`, `ralph-pi.sh`, `ralph/LOOP_CONTEXT.md`,
  `ralph/builder.md`, `tools/ralph_pi_watchdog.sh`,
  `tools/runner/test_review_state.sh`) is operator-owned and dirty in the

## Iteration 112 — batch 84: batch 83's "before" was not the parent build, and the blend change moves zero pixels

Review remediation, not a feature slice. External review
`logs/ralph-pi/run-20261106-062909/review-3.md` (on `f47d8fc..a9127fc`) carried no
Critical and no High, so nothing was mandatory — but its verdict said F1 had to be
closed before the next renderer batch, and F2–F5 were cheap and in scope. All five
are closed, and F1 closed against the project's own record.

### F1 (Medium, escalates to High if the second reading held) — CONFIRMED, and the cause is the reviewer's candidate (a): the artifact was not the parent build

The reviewer re-derived batch 83's arithmetic and found it could not come from
`f47d8fc`'s code, because every fragment-alpha source on this backend is 255 for an
unblended pass; the solved per-surface alphas (7, 8, 12, 16, 97, 113, 133, 135, 137,
157, 163, 168, 188, 223 / 255) demanded an alpha source the reading did not show. Two
candidates were offered: a stale `before` artifact, or a live sub-255 alpha. Neither
is answerable from the source, which is what made it a measurement.

**The measurement.** Built the parent clean in a throwaway worktree and ran it through
the same pinned harness:

```
git worktree add /mnt/nas/Development/mdk-b84-parent f47d8fc
DEVKITPRO=/opt/devkitpro DEVKITARM=/opt/devkitpro/devkitARM \
  MDK_DATA_DIR=/mnt/nas/Development/mdk-sdl/MDK make -C mdk_3ds -j4   # md5 09ab51e1…
DISPLAY=:99 mdk_3ds/tools/emurun.sh --secs 30 --min-frames 600 --shot /tmp/mdk-b84/parent.png
```

`emurun` exit 0, Mandarine md5 `0d2adab6`, display `:99`, guest ended at frame 1680 —
the same frame the batch-83 run ended at, and the guest's own line is identical at
frame 1500 and 1680 (`feet=(0.0,4.0,0.0) yaw=90.0 eye=(0.0,-4.0,4.5)`), so the scene
is static and the wall-clock screenshot is a fair comparison. Against the 400x240
top-panel crop `(440,253)-(839,492)`:

| pair | pixels that differ, in the panel |
|---|---|
| clean `f47d8fc` build vs batch 83's `before.png` (`d6b89982…`) | **33795** |
| clean `f47d8fc` build vs batch 83's `after.png` (`0c101114…`) | **0** |
| clean `f47d8fc` build vs this batch's build (`25a56e59…`) | **0** |

Over the whole 1280x1024 capture the two builds differ by **64 pixels, all of them at
x 760..767, y 744..752** — the emulator's own `Frame: N.NN ms` overlay on the bottom
screen, which is the harness's noise floor, not the game's.

So batch 83's `after` is genuine and its `before` is not the parent. **Retracted**: the
whole before/after table — "33909 px differ, 33844 brighter and 65 darker", "the top
panel's near-clear pixels fall 68001 (71.3 %) → 58127 (61.0 %)", and the headline "a
surface the palette says is (255,0,0) was landing at (30,30,45) = src*(16/255) +
clear*(1-16/255)". Those numbers compare the batch-83 build with some build that is
not `f47d8fc`. The reviewer's solve was right — 32128 of the 33909 changed pixels do
fit `before = a·after + (1−a)·clear` with a constant `a` per surface, re-derived here
independently before any capture was taken — which is exactly why the contradiction
was real and why only an artifact check could settle it.

**And the alpha question is closed by measurement, not by reading.** The parent blends
with `SRC_ALPHA / ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA` and this build replaces; two different register
states agreeing across 96000 pixels means every visible fragment has alpha 255. There
is no sub-255 fragment alpha in this scene, so candidate (b) — a sub-255 source still
live on `Pass::Blended` — does not survive. The code reading agrees: the expansion
forces 255 on every non-zero index (`renderer_c3d.cpp:1267`), and the flat-colour path
carries the material alpha, which is 1.0 for a palette colour (`material_resolver.cpp:93-96`)
and the DTI glass alpha only on a `Blended` pass, where the oracle multiplies it in
(`shaders/palette.hlsl` returns `float4(palette…rgb, 1.0) * colour * input.colour`).

**What batch 83 still stands on.** The citro3d register state (its `C3D_Init` calls
`C3D_AlphaBlend(ADD, ADD, SRC_ALPHA, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA, SRC_ALPHA,

## Iteration 113 — batch 85: review-4 remediation — the enum guard could not fail, and now the compiler owns it

**Review remediated:** `logs/ralph-pi/run-20261106-062909/review-4.md` (DeepSeek
V4.1 Flash TH, proved cross-family). No Critical and no High; nine findings, F1–F9,
all dispositioned below. The batch is the remediation itself plus the emulator
evidence its one shipped-code change needs (AGENTS P8).

### What changed, and the reference it satisfies

* **`mdk_core/src/render/render_types.h`** — `mdk::Pass` gains a `Count` sentinel.
  The oracle's enum is six members (`src/Mdk.Engine/Render/Renderer.cs:34-48`), and
  the sentinel does not change any existing member's ordinal, so no golden, no
  parity gate and no wire value moves.
* **`mdk_core/src/render/draw_queue.h`** — `kDrawQueuePassCount` is now
  `static_cast<int32_t>(Pass::Count)` instead of a hand-counted `6`. Same defect
  class as F1: with the literal, a seventh pass would have been accepted by the
  enum, rejected by `draw_queue.cpp:32,48`'s bounds check, and its draws would
  have vanished with nothing to say so.
* **`mdk_3ds/src/render/pica_matrix.{h,cpp}`** — the replace pair is a named
  constant `kBlendReplace = {false, ONE, ZERO, ONE, ZERO}`; `blendStateForPass`
  returns it for the four opaque passes; `depthStateForPass` names `Pass::Count`
  so its switch stays exhaustive without a `default` and `-Wswitch` remains the
  backstop; `alphaTestPasses`'s comment now says which instrument holds what.
* **`mdk_3ds/src/render/renderer_c3d.cpp`** — `installBlendState` reads
  `BlendState::enable` (one call site kept, because the frame gate counts them);
  the diagnostic-triangle comment's 13/58 probe numbers become Iteration 108's
  69/201; the alpha-test comment's "TWO CORNERS" becomes THREE with the
  `enhanced.hlsl` canvas/image branch.
* **`tests/scripts/pica_matrix_tests.cpp`** — three `static_assert`s replace the
  tautology; `tests/scripts/tick1.cpp` — `passName` names `Count`.
* **`docs/CONTINUATION.md`** — the F8 wording, this batch's state, three new owner
  actions, two new standing facts.

### Findings: fixed, with the evidence

**F1 (Medium, confirmed) — FIXED.** The reviewer was right and the check it
condemned was this loop's own: `bool coversAll = sizeof(every)/sizeof(every[0]) == 6;`
is `6 == 6` whatever the enum holds, and the loop then sampled exactly the six
members it was handed. The fix is the reviewer's first option — the compiler owns
the claim now — and it was demonstrated rather than asserted: inserting
`Fancy,` before `Count` and recompiling `pica_matrix_tests.cpp` fails three times,

    pica_matrix_tests.cpp:409:54: error: static assertion failed: mdk::Pass no longer
      has the six members the oracle's enum has (src/Mdk.Engine/Render/Renderer.cs:34-48)...
    pica_matrix_tests.cpp:414:52: error: static assertion failed: this array must name
      every mdk::Pass member: that is the whole of the coverage claim, so the compiler
      has to hold it
    pica_matrix_tests.cpp:418:54: error: static assertion failed: the unblended set is
      the oracle's NOT (Blended or Overlay), so it is every pass but two

and the enumerator was then removed (the file is byte-identical to the shipped
version; `git diff` for that header is the sentinel and its comment, nothing else).
The second option — an exhaustive `switch` under `-Werror=switch` — was not taken
because neither build uses `-Werror`, so it would have been a warning, and a
warning is what the batch is replacing.

**F6 (Low, confirmed) — FIXED in code, and measured.** `installBlendState`
installs `mdk::pica::kBlendReplace` whenever `enable` is false, so the struct
cannot claim "disabled" and mix anyway. The claim "this removes a way of being
wrong and changes no register value any pass installs today" was tested rather than
argued, with a clean worktree build of the parent:

    parent  4839cc1, /tmp/mdk-b85-parent, mdk.3dsx md5 238051c6f5d856e3e8888bc5c77360ab
            guest frame 2280, capture sha256 45756746b73f4354…
    current batch 85 as shipped, mdk.3dsx md5 9dfed8e081cfb95e58cadc252d691444
            guest frame 2220, capture sha256 defc81451ea88801…
    panel crop (440,253)-(839,492), 400x240:  0 px differ
      both panels' pixels hash to 784fad63a8a72999c8585720276a454b249a96ba1dab7c6adbc761816ff446a9
    whole capture: 58 px, all of them x 753..760, y 744..752 — Mandarine's own
      `Frame: N.NN ms` overlay on the BOTTOM screen, the documented noise floor
    A third build of the same code, taken before a whitespace-only comment
    realignment (md5 8308388be3e7f63b33a1023fd8448a9b, frame 2280), gives the same
    panel again, so the pair does not rest on which of the two was captured.

Pair, commands, display and hashes: `docs/evidence/2026-11-06-L7-blend-enable-{parent,current}.{png,txt}`.
What the pair cannot say is written in both sidecars: the scene is 154 all-`Solid`
batches, so no blended pass is exercised by either half.

**F5, F7, F9 (Low, confirmed) — FIXED as comments, which is what they are.** F5:
the predicate's comment claimed a coupling that does not exist — the backend writes
a literal `C3D_AlphaTest(true, GPU_GREATER, mdk::pica::kAlphaTestReference)` and
never calls `alphaTestPasses`; only the reference is shared. Making the claim true
by routing the renderer through the predicate would break the frame gate's
`alpha-test-is-the-oracles-discard` arm, which exists precisely because the
spelling is the only pin, so the comment now names the instrument that holds the
spelling (`c3d_frame_test.sh`'s `alpha-test-reference-moved` and
`alpha-test-disabled` arms, both demonstrated red by the arm runner). F7: the
renderer comment's "cull NONE changes the frame by 13 px, depth off by 58" is
Iteration 108's 69/201 now, cited at the site. F9: `shaders/enhanced.hlsl:199-201`
returns `float4(..., texel.a) * colour` for `MODE_CANVAS`/`MODE_IMAGE`, so a canvas
texel of alpha 0 is painted by the oracle and discarded by this frame-wide test —
and unlike the other two corners its alpha is not forced to 0/255 by the palette
expansion. Recorded as the third corner and repeated in NEXT under item 5b, since
the canvas is the blocked HUD seam.

**F8 (Low, confirmed) — FIXED in `docs/CONTINUATION.md`.** The claim was load-bearing
and the comparison was not: 58464 exact clear pixels of 96000 is not the same
quantity as the census's 58522 near-clear of a 95361-px panel at another frame with
another tolerance. The wording is now the equality that carries the argument — the
count is 58464 in both builds — and the "61 % stands" cross-comparison is gone.

### Findings: not builder-actionable, recorded with the reason

**F2 (Medium).** Both facts are confirmed: `tools/check.sh:175` runs
`gates_batch_integrity.py` with neither `--staged` nor `--base`, so a PROTECTED
worktree edit is invisible to the loop's own gate; and `ralph/builder.md` is in the
`PROTECTED` set at `gates_batch_integrity.py:12-26`. The reviewer's open question —
who owns the six dirty files — is answerable from the tree, and the answer is the
operator, so this is a gate gap and not a contract breach: the diffs are harness
policy no batch writes (reviewer/worker chains, `ITER_TIMEOUT`/`REVIEW_TIMEOUT`,
`PI_CMD=/mnt/nas/Development/qwen-slot-pi.sh`, the watchdog's phase limits, a
"Search scope" section in the builder's own contract), batches 83/84/85 each staged
none of them, and this batch staged its paths by name and did not use the add-all
commit path. The fix is not available to a builder: the two files that would carry
it, `tools/check.sh` and `tools/runner/gates_batch_integrity.py`, are both
`PROTECTED`. Owner action recorded with the suggested change (`--staged` when the
index is non-empty) and with the `test_review_state.sh` mode bit (100755→100644,
and this uid does not own the file so it cannot chmod it either).

**F3 (Medium).** Confirmed contradiction, owner decision required, and all three
files are operator-owned and uncommitted: the edited directive asserts "the `-th` ->
`flash` pair is the single operator-approved same-family exception", `ralph-pi.sh`
asserts "No independence exception appears anywhere in this file: none is needed, and
one must not be added", and `test_review_state.sh` still pins the refusal (it passes
right now, which is the proof that the code and the test are the pair that agree and
the directive is the outlier). The sibling-repository claim was checked and the
reviewer is right that it needs correcting. A builder must not resolve a
protected-directive contradiction, and `AGENTS.md`'s review-independence rule is the
one thing in this loop that must not be relaxed by the party it constrains.

**F4 (Medium).** Confirmed: `guard()`'s `exit 3` became an unbounded
`while :; … sleep 300`, and `phase route-health` is rewritten before every round, so
the watchdog's `route-health|startup|verify) limit=900` arm compares against a
refreshed epoch and can never fire; `logs/ralph/disabled` is already touched, so the
loop would be parked and silent. The wait is a deliberate operator decision — the
file's own comment says a single builder route must be waited out, not exited on —
and both files are operator-owned and uncommitted, so the builder's contribution is
the bound the reviewer suggested (a `route-dead` phase no watchdog arm covers, or
stop refreshing the epoch on a failed round), recorded as an owner action. Note also
the standing fact: editing `ralph-pi.sh` does not change the running loop.
